citations.quote:
Fix a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$ of type
$A_{n-1}$ with Cartan $\mathfrak h$, positive system $\Phi^+$, Weyl vector
$\rho$, Weyl group $W$ (identified with $S_n$) and dot action
$w\cdot\lambda=w(\lambda+\rho)-\rho$. Fix a dominant regular integral weight
$\lambda$, i.e. $\langle\lambda+\rho,\alpha^\vee\rangle\neq0$ for every root and
$\lambda$ integral, and let $\mathcal O_\lambda$ be the corresponding regular
integral block in the conventions of
[[def-regular-integral-category-o-block-and-its-antidominant-weight]]: standard
objects $\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)=M(w\cdot\lambda)$, simples $L(w\cdot\lambda)$,
indecomposable projectives $P(w\cdot\lambda)$ for $w\in W$, with
$\lambda=e\cdot\lambda$ the unique dominant and $w_0\cdot\lambda$ the unique
antidominant element and $\Delta(w_0\cdot\lambda)=L(w_0\cdot\lambda)$.

This item freezes the following conventions, each inherited from the cited
suppliers and used verbatim below.

(i) **Multiplicity conventions.** $(P(w\cdot\lambda):\Delta(y\cdot\lambda))$ is
the Verma-flag multiplicity of [[def-verma-flag-and-its-multiplicities]] and
$[M(y\cdot\lambda):L(w\cdot\lambda)]$ the composition multiplicity, and
$$(P(w\cdot\lambda):\Delta(y\cdot\lambda))=[M(y\cdot\lambda):L(w\cdot\lambda)]$$
by BGG reciprocity ([[thm-bgg-reciprocity]]).

(ii) **Bruhat reversal convention.** Along the bijection
$W\ni w\mapsto w\cdot\lambda$ the Bruhat order runs opposite to the dominance
order, in the two exact senses used on this page: $y\le w$ implies
$w\cdot\lambda\le y\cdot\lambda$ in the dominance order, and every nonzero
multiplicity forces the index direction, i.e.
$[M(y\cdot\lambda):L(w\cdot\lambda)]\neq0$ implies $y\le w$ in the Bruhat
order. The first sense is the inclusion direction of
[[lem-dominant-integral-dot-translates-embed-in-the-verma-module]] (for
$w\ge y$ one has $M(w\cdot\lambda)\subseteq M(y\cdot\lambda)$, so the highest
weight of the submodule is the lower one), and the second is
[[lem-jordan-holder-factors-of-verma-modules-lie-above-the-head]], which
confines every composition factor of $M(y\cdot\lambda)$ to labels
$w\ge y$. The full statement that the two orders are isomorphic as posets is
not needed here and is not asserted; only these two directions, together with
the finiteness of intervals of the Bruhat order
([[lem-bruhat-order-basic-properties-for-permutations]]), are used.

(iii) **Hecke and Kazhdan–Lusztig normalization.** The Kazhdan–Lusztig basis
$\underline H_w=\sum_{y\le w}p_{y,w}H_y$ of the normalized type-$A$ Hecke
algebra ([[thm-existence-and-uniqueness-of-the-kazhdan-lusztig-basis]]), with
$$p_{y,w}=v^{\ell(w)-\ell(y)}P_{y,w}(v^{-2})$$
in the classical $q=v^{-2}$ normalization
([[def-kazhdan-lusztig-polynomials-in-the-classical-q-normalization]]), support
$p_{y,w}=0$ unless $y\le w$, diagonal $p_{w,w}=1$, and simultaneous inversion
symmetry $p_{y^{-1},w^{-1}}=p_{y,w}$.

(iv) **Soergel label and character dictionary.** Write $R_x$ for the
polynomial standard graph bimodule supported at $x$, and $B_x$ for the
normalized indecomposable polynomial Soergel bimodule, which is generally not a
standard graph bimodule. With right reduction $\bar B=B\otimes_S\mathbb C$
and left coinvariant-module values of $V$, the projective dictionary is
$$V(P(w\cdot\lambda))\cong\bar B_{w^{-1}}$$
([[thm-indecomposable-projectives-correspond-to-indecomposable-soergel-modules]]).
The graph label $x$ corresponds to the standard
$\Delta(x^{-1}\cdot\lambda)$. The individual support ranks are measured on the
polynomial lift before reduction, as in
[[prop-verma-flag-multiplicities-are-standard-filtration-ranks-under-v]];
no separated graph-support filtration of the reduced module is asserted.

For degree bookkeeping use precisely the standard-generator normalization of
[[def-type-a-standard-graph-bimodules-support-filtrations-and-character]]:
$\Delta_x(d)=R_x(d-\ell(x))$, and $r_{x,d}(B)$ counts these normalized polynomial
standard layers. Thus the coefficient polynomial is
$$m_x(B;v):=\sum_d r_{x,d}(B)v^d,\qquad h_\Delta(B)=\sum_xm_x(B;v)\widetilde T_x,\qquad\widetilde T_x=v^{\ell(x)}T_x.$$
Here $\widetilde T_x$ is the normalized **standard** Hecke element $H_x$ used
in clause (iii) and
[[def-normalized-type-a-hecke-algebra-and-its-bar-involution]]. The published
Soergel split-Grothendieck-ring convention instead names its simple
Kazhdan--Lusztig generators $H_i=v(T_i+1)=\widetilde T_{s_i}+v$; these must not
be confused with the standard element $H_{s_i}=vT_i$
([[thm-split-grothendieck-group-of-the-soergel-category-is-the-type-a-hecke-algebra]]).
The standard-character supplier
[[lem-the-type-a-standard-character-is-multiplicative]] identifies $h_\Delta$
with that split-Grothendieck-ring isomorphism. This records the coefficient
normalization, and does not infer the image of a general indecomposable $B_x$
by multiplying simple generators. In particular the character theorem must be
used to identify $h_\Delta(B_x)$ with $\underline H_x$; a product of simple
Soergel classes is a Bott--Samelson class and need not be $[B_x]$.
The inverse labels and all rank comparisons above use auxiliary polynomial
gradings only; forgetting them gives the ordinary projective dictionary.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathfrak g$ be a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra with Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak h$, a chosen positive-root system and corresponding Borel, Weyl group $W$, and half-sum $\rho$ of positive roots. Let $\chi_\lambda$ and $\chi_\mu$ be the central characters obtained from highest weights $\lambda,\mu\in\mathfrak h^*$ for this Borel. Then

$$\chi_\lambda=\chi_\mu \quad \text{if and only if} \quad \mu\in W\cdot \lambda,$$

where $W\cdot \lambda:=\{w(\lambda+\rho)-\rho : w\in W\}$.

For $\lambda\in\mathfrak h^*$, the **Verma module** is the induced
$\mathfrak g$-module

$$M(\lambda):=U(\mathfrak g)\otimes_{U(\mathfrak b)}\mathbb C_\lambda,$$

where $U(\mathfrak g)$ is the quotient algebra of
[[def-universal-enveloping-algebra-as-a-tensor-quotient]] and
$\mathbb C_\lambda$ is [[def-one-dimensional-borel-module-of-weight-lambda]].
Write $v_\lambda:=1\otimes c_\lambda$.  Thus $M(\lambda)$ is the quotient of
$U(\mathfrak g)$ by the left ideal generated by $x$ for $x\in\mathfrak n^+$
and $h-\lambda(h)$ for $h\in\mathfrak h$; in particular,
$\mathfrak n^+v_\lambda=0$ and $hv_\lambda=\lambda(h)v_\lambda$.

Multiplication gives a vector-space isomorphism

$$U(\mathfrak n^-)\xrightarrow{\sim}M(\lambda),\qquad u\longmapsto uv_\lambda.$$

Consequently, ordered negative-root PBW monomials from
[[thm-pbw-ordered-monomial-basis-for-the-enveloping-algebra]] applied to
$v_\lambda$ form a basis.

Assume the Axiom of Choice.

If $\langle\lambda+\rho,\alpha^\vee\rangle<0$ for every $\alpha\in\Phi^+$, then $M(\lambda)$ is simple. Thus every regular antidominant weight, in this explicit sense, has simple Verma module.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\Gamma$ be a
finite downward-closed ideal of a linkage class $C$
([[def-truncated-category-o-at-a-finite-weight-ideal]]) and let
$\lambda\in\Gamma$ be maximal in $\Gamma$. Then $\Delta(\lambda)=M(\lambda)$
is a projective object of the truncation $\mathcal O_\Gamma$
([[def-projective-object]]).

More precisely, for every $X\in\mathcal O_\Gamma$ evaluation at the
highest-weight generator $v_\lambda$ is a natural isomorphism
$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_\Gamma}(M(\lambda),X)\to
X^{\mathfrak n^+}_\lambda=X_\lambda$, and $X\mapsto X_\lambda$ is exact, so
$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_\Gamma}(M(\lambda),-)$ is exact.

Under the fixed positive-Borel convention the essential hypothesis is
maximality of $\lambda$ in the finite ideal $\Gamma$: maximality, not any
antidominance or sufficient-positivity condition, is what makes every
$\lambda$-weight vector singular. For a weight $\lambda$ that is not maximal
in $\Gamma$, $\Delta(\lambda)$ need not be projective in $\mathcal O_\Gamma$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Every simple object
$L(\mu)$ of $\mathcal O$ admits a projective cover
$P(\mu)\twoheadrightarrow L(\mu)$
([[def-essential-epimorphism-and-projective-cover]]), which may be chosen
inside the linkage class of $\mu$; the cover is unique up to isomorphism and
indecomposable. Consequently $\mathcal O$ has enough projectives: every object
of $\mathcal O$ is a quotient of a finite direct sum of such projective
covers, because objects of $\mathcal O$ have finite length and each composition
factor is a quotient of its projective cover.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). For all weights
$\lambda$ and $\mu$,
$$(P(\lambda):\Delta(\mu))=[\Delta(\mu):L(\lambda)]=[M(\mu):L(\lambda)],$$
where $P(\lambda)$ is the projective cover of $L(\lambda)$, the left-hand
multiplicity is the Verma-flag multiplicity of
[[thm-projectives-in-category-o-have-verma-flags]], and the right-hand
multiplicity is the simple composition multiplicity of the Verma module
$M(\mu)$ ([[def-standard-and-costandard-objects-in-category-o]]).

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\lambda\in\Lambda^+$ and $w\in W$. If a simple module $L(\mu)$ occurs in a composition series of $M(w\circ\lambda)$, then $\mu=u\circ\lambda$ for some $u\ge w$ in Bruhat order; moreover $L(w\circ\lambda)$ occurs exactly once. Consequently every composition factor of $M(w\circ\lambda)$ has length at least $\ell(w)$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Work in category
$\mathcal O$ with the conventions of the preceding definitions. For a weight
$\lambda$ write $\chi_\lambda$ for the generalized central character obtained
from $\lambda$, so that $\chi_\lambda=\chi_\mu$ if and only if
$\mu\in W\mathbin\cdot\lambda$
([[cor-central-characters-are-dot-weyl-orbits]]), and let
$\mathcal O=\bigoplus_\chi\mathcal O_\chi$ be the central-character
decomposition of [[thm-category-o-decomposes-by-generalized-central-character]]
with inclusions $\operatorname{incl}_\chi$ and exact projections
$\operatorname{pr}_\chi$, so that
$\operatorname{pr}_\chi\circ\operatorname{incl}_\chi=\operatorname{id}$.

For a finite-dimensional $\mathfrak h$-semisimple $\mathfrak g$-module $E$
([[def-weight-and-weight-space-of-a-lie-algebra-representation]]) and two
generalized central characters $\chi,\chi'$, set
$$T_{\chi,E,\chi'}:=\operatorname{pr}_{\chi'}\circ(E\otimes-)\circ\operatorname{incl}_\chi\colon\mathcal O_\chi\longrightarrow\mathcal O_{\chi'}.$$
This is well defined because $E\otimes-$ is an exact endofunctor of
$\mathcal O$
([[prop-tensoring-with-a-finite-dimensional-module-preserves-category-o]])
and the projections and inclusions are exact.

For weights $\lambda,\mu$ with $\mu-\lambda$ integral
([[def-dot-action-facets-and-single-wall-translation-data]]), let $\nu$ be the
unique dominant weight in the linear Weyl orbit $W(\mu-\lambda)$, which exists
and is unique by [[lem-finite-weyl-closed-chambers-and-stabilizers]] and is
integral; let $L(\nu)$ be the finite-dimensional simple module of highest
weight $\nu$
([[thm-finite-dimensional-simple-modules-are-classified-by-dominant-highest-weights]]).
Define
$$T_\lambda^\mu:=T_{\chi_\lambda,L(\nu),\chi_\mu}\colon\mathcal O_{\chi_\lambda}\longrightarrow\mathcal O_{\chi_\mu},\qquad T_\mu^\lambda:=T_{\chi_\mu,L(\nu)^*,\chi_\lambda}\colon\mathcal O_{\chi_\mu}\longrightarrow\mathcal O_{\chi_\lambda},$$
where $L(\nu)^*$ is the ordinary linear dual, a finite-dimensional
$\mathfrak h$-semisimple simple module isomorphic to $L(-w_0\nu)$ by
[[prop-highest-weight-of-the-dual-representation]].

The labels $\lambda$ and $\mu$ denote actual weights and not $\rho$-shifted
parameters. The central-character subcategories used here are those of the
published decomposition; a central-character summand can contain several
linkage blocks of
[[thm-central-character-summands-split-into-linkage-blocks]], while for an
indecomposable central-character summand the present functors are translation
between that summand and its target.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\lambda,\mu$ be dominant regular integral
weights for the same complex type-$A$ semisimple Lie algebra and fixed positive
system. Let $\nu$ be the unique dominant member of $W(\mu-\lambda)$ and
$E=L(\nu)$ the finite-dimensional simple. The actual translation functors
$$F=T_\lambda^\mu=\operatorname{pr}_{\chi_\mu}(E\otimes-)\operatorname{incl}_{\chi_\lambda},\qquad G=T_\mu^\lambda=\operatorname{pr}_{\chi_\lambda}(E^*\otimes-)\operatorname{incl}_{\chi_\mu}$$
are exact mutually inverse equivalences, with natural adjunction isomorphisms
$\operatorname{Id}\cong GF$ and $FG\cong\operatorname{Id}$. They preserve the
dot-orbit labels: for every $w\in W$,
$$F\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)\cong\Delta(w\cdot\mu),\quad FL(w\cdot\lambda)\cong L(w\cdot\mu),\quad FP(w\cdot\lambda)\cong P(w\cdot\mu),$$
and conversely for $G$. Consequently the two blocks have identical Verma-flag
and composition multiplicities, both equal to $P_{y,w}(1)$, and $F$ transports
the inverse-Kazhdan–Lusztig character identity as a Grothendieck-group identity
with the same signed weighted-inverse coefficients $q'_{w,x}(1)$ and the same
support $x\ge w$. Formal characters in the two blocks use their respective
weights $x\cdot\lambda$ and $x\cdot\mu$; they need not be equal as weight
series. The dominant/antidominant, Bruhat, left/right and inverse-Soergel-label
conventions are preserved. This is an ungraded categorical transport and
supplies no Ext or Koszul grading.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $E$ be a
finite-dimensional $\mathfrak h$-semisimple $\mathfrak g$-module with weight
multiplicities $\dim E_\eta$
([[def-weight-and-weight-space-of-a-lie-algebra-representation]]). For every
weight $\mu$, the object $E\otimes\Delta(\mu)$ has a finite Verma flag
([[def-verma-flag-and-its-multiplicities]]) whose factors are $\Delta(\mu+\eta)$,
the factor $\Delta(\mu+\eta)$ occurring $\dim E_\eta$ times; the factors can be
ordered so that a real-linear height $\ell$ with $\ell(\alpha_i)=1$ is nonincreasing.

Consequently, if $X\in\mathcal O$ has a finite Verma flag with multiplicities
$(X:\Delta(\nu))$, then $E\otimes X$ has a finite Verma flag and
$$(E\otimes X:\Delta(\mu))=\sum_\eta\dim E_\eta\,(X:\Delta(\mu-\eta)).$$

Identify $\mathbb Z[q]$ with $\mathbb Z[v^{-2}]$ by $q\mapsto v^{-2}$. For $y\le w$ in $S_n$, put $d=\ell(w)-\ell(y)$ and define the **Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomial** $P_{y,w}(q)\in\mathbb Z[q]$ by $$P_{y,w}(v^{-2})=v^{-d}p_{y,w},$$ where $\underline H_w=\sum_{y\le w}p_{y,w}H_y$ is the Kazhdan–Lusztig basis of [[lem-type-a-kazhdan-lusztig-basis-has-elementary-triangular-bar-properties]]. The parity clause of that theorem makes the right side a polynomial in $v^{-2}$. The conventions are: $P_{y,w}=0$ unless $y\le w$, $P_{w,w}=1$, $P_{y,w}$ has constant term 1, and for $y<w$ its degree is at most $(\ell(w)-\ell(y)-1)/2$. The **$\mu$-coefficient** is $$\mu(y,w):=	ext{coefficient of }q^{(\ell(w)-\ell(y)-1)/2}	ext{ in }P_{y,w},$$ defined to be 0 when $\ell(w)-\ell(y)$ is even; equivalently $\mu(y,w)$ is the coefficient of $v$ in $p_{y,w}$. One writes $\mu(y|w)
e0$ when $y
e w$ and ($y<w$ and $\mu(y,w)
e0$) or ($w<y$ and $\mu(w,y)
e0$). The dictionary with the literature is recorded for use: with the classical parameter $T_s^2=(q-1)T_s+q$ one has $H_w=v^{\ell(w)}T_w$, the element $\underline H_w$ is the basis element $C'_w$ of [EW], and $h_{y,w}=p_{y,w}$ with $v^{\ell(w)-\ell(y)}P_{y,w}(v^{-2})=h_{y,w}$ [EW, Remark 3.2].

Assume the Axiom of Choice. In a regular integral type-$A$ block
$\mathcal O_\lambda$, for every $w\in W$ the class of $L(w\cdot\lambda)$ in the
Grothendieck group, equivalently its formal character, is
$$[L(w\cdot\lambda)]=\sum_{x\in W}q'_{w,x}(1)\,[M(x\cdot\lambda)],\qquad\text{i.e.}\qquad \mathrm{ch}\,L(w\cdot\lambda)=\sum_{x\in W}q'_{w,x}(1)\,\mathrm{ch}\,M(x\cdot\lambda),$$
where $q'_{x,w}$ are the inverse Kazhdan–Lusztig coefficients of
[[def-inverse-kazhdan-lusztig-polynomials]] ($Q'=P^{-1}$, $q'_{x,w}\in v\mathbb Z[v]$
for $x<w$, $q'_{w,w}=1$) and the sum is supported on $x\ge w$. Equivalently, in
the signed normalization $q_{x,w}=\mathrm{sgn}(x)\mathrm{sgn}(w)q'_{x,w}$ the
formula is the signed inverse-Kazhdan–Lusztig sum
$$\mathrm{ch}\,L(w\cdot\lambda)=\sum_{x\ge w}(-1)^{\ell(w)-\ell(x)}q_{w,x}(1)\,\mathrm{ch}\,M(x\cdot\lambda).$$
The coefficients $q'_{w,x}(1)$ are the weighted incidence-algebra inverse of
$(P_{y,z}(1))$, given by the finite signed chain sum of products of
$P_{y,z}(1)$; they are integers that may be negative. They specialize to
ordinary Bruhat Möbius values on intervals where every comparable-pair
Kazhdan–Lusztig value is $1$, but not in general. Only the value at $q=1$
occurs.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). For every dominant
integral weight $\lambda\in\Lambda^+$, the character of the finite-dimensional
simple module $L(\lambda)$ is
$$\operatorname{ch}L(\lambda)=A(\lambda+\rho)\cdot A(\rho)^{-1}=\Bigl(\sum_{w\in W}(-1)^{\ell(w)}e^{w(\lambda+\rho)}\Bigr)\Big/\Bigl(e^{\rho}\prod_{\alpha\in\Phi^+}(1-e^{-\alpha})\Bigr),$$
the quotient being taken in the completed character ring $\mathcal R$ of
[[def-completed-formal-character-ring-for-downward-cones]], where
$A(\rho)$ is invertible with inverse
$e^{-\rho}\prod_{\alpha\in\Phi^+}(1-e^{-\alpha})^{-1}$
([[thm-weyl-denominator-identity]],
[[lem-geometric-series-invertibility-in-the-completed-character-ring]]). No
quotient of ordinary functions is intended before this formal cancellation is
justified.

derivations.claim: **The two blocks.** With $\rho=1$ the dot action on coordinates is $s\cdot l=s(l+1)-1=-l-2$, so the orbit of $n$ is $\{n,-n-2\}$; a weight $l$ is dominant regular integral exactly when $l\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}$, and then $-n-2<n$ in the dominance order. Hence $C_n$ is a regular integral block with the two labels $e=123\mapsto n$ and $s=213\mapsto-n-2$; for $n=0$ and $n=1$ the abstract labelled data are the same, which is what makes the two blocks directly comparable.

**The PBW computation.** Fix $n\ge0$ and put $v_k:=f^kv_n$, a basis of $M(n)$ by [F2]; the highest weight vector $v_0$ generates $M(n)$ and spans the $n$-weight space, which is one-dimensional. From the $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ relations $[h,f]=-2f$, $[e,f]=h$ one computes $h\cdot v_k=(n-2k)v_k$, $f\cdot v_k=v_{k+1}$, and, by induction on $k$ from $e\cdot v_0=0$, $e\cdot v_k=k(n-k+1)v_{k-1}$. If $M(n)=A\oplus B$ with $v_0=a+b$, then $a$ and $b$ lie in the one-dimensional weight space $M(n)_n=\mathbb Cv_0$; if $b\ne0$ then $b$ is a nonzero multiple of $v_0$, so $v_0\in B$ and $M(n)=U(\mathfrak g)v_0\subseteq B$, while if $b=0$ then $v_0=a\in A$ and $M(n)\subseteq A$; either way one of the summands is zero. So $M(n)$ is indecomposable.

**The submodule $W$.** Let $W:=\operatorname{span}\{v_k:k\ge n+1\}$. By step 1.2 it is stable under $f$ and $h$; and $e\cdot v_{n+1}=(n+1)(n-(n+1)+1)v_n=0$, while for $k\ge n+2$ one has $e\cdot v_k=k(n-k+1)v_{k-1}$ with $k-1\ge n+1$, so $e$ maps $W$ into $W$. Hence $W$ is a nonzero submodule. Its highest weight vector $v_{n+1}$ has weight $n-2(n+1)=-n-2$ and is killed by $e$; the linear map $M(-n-2)\to W$ sending the basis element $f^kv_{-n-2}$ of the PBW model of $M(-n-2)$ to $v_{n+1+k}$ is a $\mathfrak g$-module isomorphism by the action formulas of step 1.2 (both sides have the same $h$-eigenvalues and the same $e,f$-action). Since $-n-2+1=-n-1<0$, the Verma $M(-n-2)$ is simple by [F3], so $W\cong M(-n-2)=L(-n-2)$.

**Characters.** By step 1.2 the weight multiplicities of $M(n)$ are $1$ in each weight $n-2k$, $k\ge0$, so $\mathrm{ch}\,M(n)=\sum_{k\ge0}e^{n-2k}$ and $\mathrm{ch}\,M(-n-2)=\sum_{k\ge0}e^{-n-2-2k}$; the character formula of [F10] therefore gives $\mathrm{ch}\,L(n)=\mathrm{ch}\,M(n)-\mathrm{ch}\,M(-n-2)=\sum_{k=0}^{n}e^{n-2k}=e^{n}+e^{n-2}+\cdots+e^{-n}$, in agreement with the Weyl character of the finite-dimensional simple $L(n)$ by [F11], and $\mathrm{ch}\,L(-n-2)=\mathrm{ch}\,M(-n-2)$.

**The quotient is $L(n)$.** By step 1.2 the images of $v_0,\dots,v_n$ form a basis of $Q:=M(n)/W$, with weights $n,n-2,\dots,-n$, each occurring once; in particular $Q$ is finite-dimensional and nonzero with a one-dimensional $n$-weight space. By [F7] every composition factor of $M(n)$ is $L(n)$ or $L(-n-2)$, and $L(n)$ occurs exactly once. The simple $L(-n-2)=M(-n-2)$ is infinite-dimensional, because the PBW basis $\{f^kv_{-n-2}:k\ge0\}$ of $M(-n-2)$ is infinite by [F2]; hence no composition factor of the finite-dimensional module $Q$ is $L(-n-2)$, and the only remaining factor is $L(n)$, occurring once. Therefore $Q\cong L(n)$, and $M(n)$ has exactly the two composition factors $L(n)$ and $L(-n-2)$, each once.

**The projective structure.** The block $C_n=\{n,-n-2\}$ is a finite downward-closed ideal with maximum $n$; by [F4] the Verma $\Delta(n)=M(n)$ is projective in the block. Every submodule is a sum of weight spaces: polynomial interpolation in $h$ extracts the finitely many weight components of any vector. If a submodule contains $v_k$ for $0\le k\le n$, then $e^kv_k$ is a nonzero multiple of $v_0$ by step 1.2, and the submodule is all of $M(n)$. Thus every proper submodule lies in $W=\operatorname{span}\{v_k:k\ge n+1\}$, whose quotient is $L(n)$ by step 3.1; $W$, rather than all lower weight spaces, is the unique maximal submodule. A submodule mapping onto $L(n)$ contains a weight-$n$ vector and hence $v_0$, so $M(n)\twoheadrightarrow L(n)$ is essential. By uniqueness of projective covers [F5], $P(n)=P(e\cdot l)$ is isomorphic to $\Delta(n)$ and is the projective cover of $L(n)$. For the other label apply BGG reciprocity [F6]: $(P(-n-2):\Delta(n))=[M(n):L(-n-2)]=1$ and $(P(-n-2):\Delta(-n-2))=[M(-n-2):L(-n-2)]=1$ by steps 2.1 and 3.1, while all other flag multiplicities vanish since the block has only these two labels. So $P(s\cdot l)=P(-n-2)$ has a flag with the two factors $\Delta(n)$ and $\Delta(-n-2)$, each once. If its quotient factor were $\Delta(n)$, projectivity of $\Delta(n)$ would split that two-step flag, contradicting the indecomposability of $P(-n-2)$ in [F5]. Hence the submodule factor is $\Delta(n)$ and the quotient factor is $\Delta(-n-2)$, giving the short exact sequence $0\to\Delta(n)\to P(-n-2)\to\Delta(-n-2)\to0$. This sequence is nonsplit: a splitting would exhibit $P(-n-2)\cong\Delta(n)\oplus\Delta(-n-2)$ as a direct sum of two nonzero objects, contradicting the indecomposability of projective covers in [F5]. Finally $\Delta(-n-2)=M(-n-2)=L(-n-2)$ by step 2.1.

**The multiplicity data for $n=0,1$.** The four flag multiplicities of the Example are those just computed and do not depend on $n$: $(P(e\cdot l):\Delta(e\cdot l))=1$, $(P(s\cdot l):\Delta(e\cdot l))=1$, $(P(s\cdot l):\Delta(s\cdot l))=1$, $(P(e\cdot l):\Delta(s\cdot l))=0$ (the last because $P(n)\cong\Delta(n)$ has only the factor $\Delta(n)$). The composition multiplicities are likewise independent of $n$: $[M(n):L(n)]=[M(n):L(-n-2)]=[M(-n-2):L(-n-2)]=1$ and $[M(-n-2):L(n)]=0$ by steps 2.1 and 3.1, since $M(-n-2)=L(-n-2)$ is simple and its highest weight differs from $n$. For $n=0,1$ these are exactly the displayed matrices; they match $P_{e,e}=P_{e,s}=P_{s,s}=1$, $P_{s,e}=0$ by [F10], as asserted by the multiplicity theorem on the A page.

**The transported sequence.** Take the principal block $n=0$ and the target $n=1$, both dominant regular integral, and note that for $\lambda=0$, $\mu=1$ the difference $\mu-\lambda=1$ has dominant member $\nu=1$; here $E=L(1)$ is the two-dimensional simple with weights $+1,-1$, each once, and $E^*\cong E$. By [F9] the tensor $E\otimes M(0)$ has Verma flag factors $M(1)$ and $M(-1)$, and $E\otimes M(-2)$ has factors $M(-1)$ and $M(-3)$. The projections to the blocks $\chi_1$ and $\chi_0$ keep exactly the factors lying in the respective dot orbits $\{1,-3\}$ and $\{0,-2\}$ by [F1]: hence $F(M(0))=\operatorname{pr}_{\chi_1}(E\otimes M(0))\cong M(1)$ and $F(M(-2))\cong M(-3)$, while $G(M(1))=\operatorname{pr}_{\chi_0}(E\otimes M(1))\cong M(0)$ from the factors $M(2),M(0)$ and $G(M(-3))\cong M(-2)$ from the factors $M(-2),M(-4)$. By the transport theorem [F8] $F(L(0))=L(1)$, $G(L(1))=L(0)$, $F(P(0))=P(1)$, $F(P(-2))=P(-3)$ and conversely. Since $F$ is exact, applying it to the nonsplit sequence $0\to M(-2)\to M(0)\to L(0)\to0$ of the principal block produces the exact sequence $0\to F(M(-2))\to F(M(0))\to F(L(0))\to0$, that is $0\to M(-3)\to M(1)\to L(1)\to0$ in the block $C_1$; it is nonsplit because an exact inverse equivalence $G$ would carry a splitting of its image back to a splitting of the original sequence. The original middle module is $M(0)=P(0)$, not $P(-2)$; it is indecomposable by step 1.2, and its submodule $M(-2)$ and quotient $L(0)$ are both nonzero by steps 2.1 and 3.1, so such a splitting is impossible.

The claims of the Example are therefore all verified: the two blocks $C_0$ and $C_1$ share the displayed multiplicity matrices (steps 4.1 and 5.1), the projective cover $P(e\cdot l)$ equals $\Delta(e\cdot l)$ and $P(s\cdot l)$ carries the nonsplit two-step sequence with $\Delta(s\cdot l)=L(s\cdot l)$ (step 4.1), the character identities telescope to the Weyl character of the $(n+1)$-dimensional simple (step 2.2), and the actual inverse equivalences $F$ and $G$ transport the principal-block Verma sequence to $0\to M_{-3}\to M_1\to L_1\to0$ (step 5.2). The two blocks use different weight series; only the labels and the combinatorial data agree.

citations.quote: For each $w\in S_n$ there is a unique element $\underline H_w\in H_v(n)$ with (i) $\overline{\underline H_w}=\underline H_w$ and (ii) $\underline H_w\in H_w+\sum_{y<w}v\mathbb Z[v]\,H_y$ (the sum over the lower Bruhat ideal of $w$). The elements $\{\underline H_w\}_{w\in S_n}$ form an $A$-basis of $H_v(n)$, and writing $\underline H_w=\sum_{y\le w}p_{y,w}H_y$ one has $p_{w,w}=1$, $p_{y,w}=0$ unless $y\le w$, $p_{y,w}\in v\mathbb Z[v]$ for $y<w$, the bar-duality $p_{x,w}=\sum_{y}r_{x,y}\,\overline{p_{y,w}}$ (matrix form $P=R\bar P$), and the symmetry $p_{y^{-1},w^{-1}}=p_{y,w}$. Moreover for $y<w$, with $d=\ell(w)-\ell(y)$: $p_{y,w}=v^{d}+\text{terms of strictly smaller degree}$ and $p_{y,w}\in v^{d}\,\mathbb Z[v^{-2}]$; in particular every $\underline H_w$ has integer nonnegative coefficients in the standard basis with $p_{y,w}$ of fixed parity $d\bmod 2$.

Let $s=s_i$ be a simple reflection and $w\in S_n$. In the Kazhdan–Lusztig basis $\{\underline H_w\}$ of [[lem-type-a-kazhdan-lusztig-basis-has-elementary-triangular-bar-properties]]: $$\underline H_s\,\underline H_w=\begin{cases}(v+v^{-1})\,\underline H_w,&sw<w,\\[2pt] \underline H_{sw}+\displaystyle\sum_{\substack{z\in S_n\\ sz<z<w}}\mu(z,w)\,\underline H_z,&sw>w,\end{cases}$$ and symmetrically $\underline H_w\underline H_s=(v+v^{-1})\underline H_w$ if $ws<w$, $\underline H_w\underline H_s=\underline H_{ws}+\sum_{zs<z<w}\mu(z,w)\underline H_z$ if $ws>w$. Here $\mu(z,w)$ is the coefficient of $v$ in $p_{z,w}$ ([[def-kazhdan-lusztig-polynomials-in-the-classical-q-normalization]]), which can be nonzero only when $\ell(w)-\ell(z)$ is odd; the sums are finite since $S_n$ is finite. In particular $\underline H_s\underline H_s=(v+v^{-1})\underline H_s$, and $\underline H_s\underline H_w=\underline H_{sw}$ when $sw>w$ and $\ell(w)\le1$. The span conclusion is for the ascent case $sw>w$: there, $\underline H_s\underline H_w$ lies in the span of $\underline H_{sw}$ and of the $\underline H_z$ with $z<w$ and $sz<z$.

Retain the notation of
[[def-parabolic-hecke-module-and-antispherical-standard-basis]] and put
$m_x:=1\otimes H_x$, $n_x:=1\otimes H_x$ for $x\in{}^JW$, and
$C_s:=\underline H_s=H_s+v$ for $s\in S$. Then:

**(1) (Bases.)** The sets $\{m_x:x\in{}^JW\}$ and $\{n_x:x\in{}^JW\}$ are
$A$-bases of $M^J$ and $N^J$ respectively. Indeed every $w\in S_n$ factors
uniquely as $w=ly$ with $l\in W_J$, $y\in{}^JW$, length-additively, and
$\varphi_+(H_l)=v^{-\ell(l)}$ and $\varphi_-(H_l)=(-v)^{\ell(l)}$
are units of $A$, so $1\otimes H_w=\varphi_\pm(H_l)\,(1\otimes H_y)$ in both
modules.

**(2) (Right action.)** For $s\in S$ and $x\in{}^JW$,
$$m_x C_s=\begin{cases}m_{xs}+v\,m_x,&xs\in{}^JW,\ xs>x,\\ m_{xs}+v^{-1}m_x,&xs\in{}^JW,\ xs<x,\\ (v+v^{-1})m_x,&xs\notin{}^JW,\end{cases}\qquad n_xC_s=\begin{cases}n_{xs}+v\,n_x,&xs\in{}^JW,\ xs>x,\\ n_{xs}+v^{-1}n_x,&xs\in{}^JW,\ xs<x,\\ 0,&xs\notin{}^JW.\end{cases}$$

**(3) (Bar.)** The assignment $a\otimes h\mapsto \bar a\otimes\bar h$ (bar on
$A$ and the bar involution of $H_v(n)$) descends to $A$-antilinear
involutions of $M^J$ and $N^J$ that satisfy
$\overline{X\cdot h}=\overline X\cdot\bar h$ and
$$\overline{m_x}=m_x+\sum_{y<x}a_{y,x}m_y,\qquad \overline{n_x}=n_x+\sum_{y<x}b_{y,x}n_y$$
with $a_{y,x},b_{y,x}\in A$ and top coefficient
$a_{x,x}=b_{x,x}=1$.

**(4) (Parabolic property.)** If $x\in{}^JW$ and $s\in S$ with
$xs\notin{}^JW$, then $xs=rx$ for a unique simple $r\in J$ and $xs>x$.

Retain the notation of
[[def-parabolic-hecke-module-and-antispherical-standard-basis]] and
[[lem-the-parabolic-hecke-modules-have-standard-bases-actions-and-compatible-bars]].
For every $x\in{}^JW$ there is a unique $C_x\in M^J$ and a unique
$D_x\in N^J$ with (i) $\overline{C_x}=C_x$ and $\overline{D_x}=D_x$, and (ii)
$C_x\in m_x+\sum_{y<x}v\mathbb Z[v]\,m_y$ and
$D_x\in n_x+\sum_{y<x}v\mathbb Z[v]\,n_y$, the sums over the lower Bruhat
ideal of $x$ inside ${}^JW$. The sets $\{C_x\}_{x\in{}^JW}$ and
$\{D_x\}_{x\in{}^JW}$ are $A$-bases of $M^J$ and $N^J$. No coefficientwise
positivity is asserted.

Retain the notation of
[[def-parabolic-hecke-module-and-antispherical-standard-basis]] and write the
parabolic Kazhdan--Lusztig bases of
[[thm-existence-and-uniqueness-of-the-parabolic-kazhdan-lusztig-basis]] as

$$C_x=\sum_{y\le x,\ y\in{}^JW}m_{y,x}\,m_y,\qquad D_x=\sum_{y\le x,\ y\in{}^JW}n_{y,x}\,n_y,\qquad x\in{}^JW,$$

with coefficients $m_{y,x},n_{y,x}\in\mathbb Z[v]$ supported on the lower
Bruhat ideal, $m_{x,x}=n_{x,x}=1$ and $m_{y,x},n_{y,x}\in v\mathbb Z[v]$ for
$y<x$.

The **spherical parabolic Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomials** are
$$M^J_{y,x}(q):=v^{-\ell(x)+\ell(y)}m_{y,x},\qquad q=v^{-2},$$
and the **antispherical (sign) parabolic Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomials** are
$$N^J_{y,x}(q):=v^{-\ell(x)+\ell(y)}n_{y,x}.$$
The parity and degree bounds established in
[[thm-parabolic-kazhdan-lusztig-polynomials-are-alternating-sums-of-ordinary-ones]]
make these polynomials in $q$; that reduction theorem discharges the
well-definedness asserted here and is recorded in `justified_by`. Values at
$v=1$ are written $m_{y,x}(1)$, $n_{y,x}(1)$.

**Normalization dictionary.** With $P^J_{y,x}(u)$ the parabolic polynomials of
Deodhar (1987) attached to the subset $J$, one has
$M^J_{y,x}=P^J_{y^{-1},x^{-1}}$ for $u=-1$ and $N^J_{y,x}=P^J_{y^{-1},x^{-1}}$
for $u=q$, in the index convention of Deodhar and of the anti-spherical
category. Thus the spherical family is the $u=-1$ normalization and the
antispherical family the $u=q$ normalization; the two are not related by a
unit.

**Spherical reduction to ordinary coefficients.** If $W_J$ is finite with
longest element $w_0^J$, then
$$m_{y,x}=p_{w_0^Jy,\,w_0^Jx}\qquad\text{for all }y,x\in{}^JW,$$
where $p$ is the coefficient of the ordinary Kazhdan--Lusztig basis of
[[def-kazhdan-lusztig-polynomials-in-the-classical-q-normalization]] and
$\underline H_{w}=\sum_{y\le w}p_{y,w}H_y$ in the normalization of
[[def-normalized-type-a-hecke-algebra-and-its-bar-involution]].

Let $(S,m)$ be a finite Coxeter matrix with presented group $W$, length $\ell$ and geometric representation $\sigma:W\to\mathrm{GL}_K(E)$ as in [[def-hh-coxeter-matrix-word-group-and-length]], [[def-hh-geometric-coxeter-representation-and-roots]] and [[lem-hh-dihedral-root-recurrence-and-root-sign]], and let $J\subseteq S$.

1. **Support and reduction.** For every $w\in W$ the set $S(w)$ of letters occurring in a reduced expression of $w$ is independent of the reduced expression, and every word in $S$ representing $w$ can be transformed into a reduced expression by repeatedly deleting two letters (Tits reduction, using only letters already present). Consequently
$$W_J=\langle J\rangle=\{w\in W:S(w)\subseteq J\}.$$
2. **Intrinsic parabolic presentation.** Let $W_J^\ast$ be the group presented by the restricted Coxeter matrix $(J,m|_J)$ in the sense of [[def-hh-coxeter-matrix-word-group-and-length]]. The canonical homomorphism $W_J^\ast\to W_J$, $s\mapsto s$, is an isomorphism. Hence $(W_J,J)$ is a Coxeter system, its intrinsic length function $\ell_J$ agrees with the ambient length $\ell$ on $W_J$, and $W_J\cap S=J$.
3. **Minimal coset representatives.** Every right coset $W_J a:=\{ua:u\in W_J\}$ ($a\in W$, [[def-coset]]) has a unique element $d$ of minimal length; it is characterized by $\ell(sd)>\ell(d)$ for all $s\in J$, and it satisfies
$$\ell(ud)=\ell(u)+\ell(d)\qquad\text{for all }u\in W_J .$$
Equivalently, every $w\in W$ has a unique factorization $w=u\,d$ with $u\in W_J$ and $d$ the minimal representative of the right coset $W_J d$, and then $\ell(w)=\ell(u)+\ell(d)$. By inversion ($w\mapsto w^{-1}$ preserves lengths and interchanges the two coset families $\{W_Ja\}$ and $\{aW_J\}$), every left coset $aW_J:=\{au:u\in W_J\}$ has a unique minimal element $d$, characterized by $\ell(ds)>\ell(d)$ for all $s\in J$ and satisfying $\ell(du)=\ell(d)+\ell(u)$ for all $u\in W_J$.
4. **Type A.** Let $n\ge2$, $S=\{s_1,\dots,s_{n-1}\}$ and $m(s_i,s_j):=3$ if $|i-j|=1$, $m(s_i,s_j):=2$ if $|i-j|>1$ (a Coxeter matrix of type $A_{n-1}$). Then $s_i\mapsto(i\ i+1)$ extends to an isomorphism $W\to S_n$ (the letters $1,\dots,n$ carry the library's symmetric group by the order-preserving identification with $\{0,\dots,n-1\}$, under which $(i\ i+1)$ is the adjacent transposition $(i-1\ i)$), and for every $w\in W$,
$$\ell(w)=\operatorname{inv}\bigl(\varphi(w)\bigr),$$
the inversion number of the corresponding permutation ([[def-inversions-inversion-number-and-sign]]). In particular a word in the $s_i$ is reduced if and only if its length equals the inversion number of its value.

Let $\le$ be the rank-inequality order on the zero-based $S_n$ of [[def-bruhat-order-on-the-symmetric-group]], and identify it with the one-based realization by shifting inputs and values by $1$. (a) This order is the strong Bruhat order of type A: the transitive closure of covers $x\to tx$ where $t$ is a transposition and $\ell(tx)=\ell(x)+1$. (b) If $y\le w$ then $\ell(y)\le\ell(w)$, with equality iff $y=w$; every saturated chain has $\ell(w)-\ell(y)$ steps; and $y\le w$ iff $y^{-1}\le w^{-1}$. (c) $y\le w$ iff for every reduced expression $w=s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_k}$, $y$ is a reduced subword. (d) For every simple reflection $s$, if $y\le w$ and $\ell(sy)>\ell(y)$, then $y\le sw$; if $y\le w$ and $\ell(sw)<\ell(w)$, then $sy\le w$. (e) Every interval $[y,w]$ is finite; if $y\le w$, then $[y,w]=\{y\}\cup\bigcup_{y\to a\le w}[a,w]$.

Let $(S,m)$ be a finite Coxeter matrix, let $W$ be the presented group with
length function $\ell$ ([[def-hh-coxeter-matrix-word-group-and-length]]), and
let $T=\{wsw^{-1}:w\in W,\ s\in S\}$ be the set of reflections of $W$
([[def-cg-canonical-reflection-homomorphism]]). Throughout, $I$ and $J$ denote
subsets of $S$.

**(1) Standard parabolic subgroups.** For $I\subseteq S$ put

$$W_I:=\langle s:s\in I\rangle\le W,$$

the subgroup generated by $I$ ([[def-generated-subgroup]]); $W_I$ is the
**standard parabolic subgroup** of $(W,S)$ of type $I$. Thus
$W_\emptyset=\{1\}$ and $W_S=W$. By
[[thm-hh-parabolic-minimal-representatives-and-length-additivity]] (1),(2): for
every $w\in W$ one has $w\in W_I$ if and only if $S(w)\subseteq I$, where
$S(w)$ is the (well-defined) set of letters of any reduced expression of $w$;
$(W_I,I)$ is a Coxeter system; its intrinsic length function agrees with
$\ell|_{W_I}$; and $W_I\cap S=I$.

**(2) Descents and the one-sided quotients.** For $w\in W$ put

$$D_L(w):=\{s\in S:\ell(sw)<\ell(w)\},\qquad D_R(w):=\{s\in S:\ell(ws)<\ell(w)\};$$

each of $\ell(sw)-\ell(w)$ and $\ell(ws)-\ell(w)$ lies in $\{\pm1\}$
([[thm-hh-coxeter-exchange-deletion-and-faithfulness]] (1)). Define

$$W^I:=\{w\in W:\ell(ws)>\ell(w)\text{ for all }s\in I\}=\{w\in W:D_R(w)\cap I=\emptyset\},$$

$${}^IW:=\{w\in W:\ell(sw)>\ell(w)\text{ for all }s\in I\}=\{w\in W:D_L(w)\cap I=\emptyset\}.$$

Conventions are fixed here: in ${}^IW$ the subset $I$ is tested on the left, in
$W^I$ it is tested on the right; $\ell(sw)$ means left multiplication by $s$
and $\ell(ws)$ right multiplication. The interpretation of these sets as sets
of coset representatives is not part of the definition; it is quoted from
[[thm-hh-parabolic-minimal-representatives-and-length-additivity]] (3) and
re-examined in [[thm-cg-parabolic-intersections-and-coset-factorization]] (3):
every $w\in W$ has a unique factorization

$$w=u\,d\qquad(u\in W_I,\ d\in{}^IW),\qquad \ell(w)=\ell(u)+\ell(d),$$

where $d$ is the unique element of minimal length in the right coset $W_Iw$, and
it satisfies $\ell(ud)=\ell(u)+\ell(d)$ for all $u\in W_I$; symmetrically every
$w\in W$ has a unique factorization

$$w=d\,v\qquad(d\in W^I,\ v\in W_I),\qquad \ell(w)=\ell(d)+\ell(v),$$

where $d$ is the unique element of minimal length in the left coset $wW_I$, and
it satisfies $\ell(dv)=\ell(d)+\ell(v)$ for all $v\in W_I$. Thus ${}^IW$
consists exactly of the elements of minimal length in the right cosets
$W_Iw=\{uw:u\in W_I\}$ and $W^I$ consists exactly of the elements of minimal
length in the sets $wW_I=\{wv:v\in W_I\}$. Inversion gives
$W^I=({}^IW)^{-1}$, because $\ell(x)=\ell(x^{-1})$ and $(sw)^{-1}=w^{-1}s$.

**(3) The two-sided quotients.** Define

$${}^IW^J:={}^IW\cap W^J=\{w\in W:\ell(sw)>\ell(w)\text{ for all }s\in I\ \text{ and }\ \ell(ws)>\ell(w)\text{ for all }s\in J\};$$

thus ${}^\emptyset W^J=W^J$, ${}^IW^\emptyset={}^IW$ and ${}^\emptyset
W^\emptyset=W$, and the members of ${}^IW^J$ are exactly the elements of $W$
with no left descent in $I$ and no right descent in $J$. Whether ${}^IW^J$ is a
set of representatives of the double cosets $W_IwW_J$ is again a theorem, not a
definition; it is proved in
[[thm-cg-double-coset-unique-minimum-and-normal-form]].

**(4) Parabolic subgroups and reflection subgroups.** A subgroup $H\le W$ is a
**parabolic subgroup** of $(W,S)$ if

$$H=wW_Iw^{-1}\qquad\text{for some }w\in W,\ I\subseteq S;$$

a parabolic subgroup with $w=1$ is *standard*. A subgroup $H\le W$ is a
**reflection subgroup** if $H=\langle H\cap T\rangle$, i.e. if $H$ is generated
by the reflections it contains. Every parabolic subgroup is a reflection
subgroup, since $wW_Iw^{-1}=\langle wsw^{-1}:s\in I\rangle$ and
$wsw^{-1}\in T$ for all $s\in S$, $w\in W$. No converse is asserted: it is not
claimed here that a subgroup generated by reflections is parabolic, and the
companion examples page computes test cases for the two distinctions created by
this definition --- standard parabolic versus parabolic, and reflection subgroup
versus parabolic subgroup.

derivations.claim: **The antispherical image.** Let $\Phi:H_v(n)\to N^J=A\otimes_{H_J}H_v(n)$, $\Phi(h):=1\otimes h$. It is $A$-linear and satisfies $\Phi(\bar h)=\overline{\Phi(h)}$ by [F3]. Since $\underline H_x$ is bar-fixed, so is $\Phi(\underline H_x)$; expanding $\underline H_x=\sum_{w\le x}p_{w,x}H_w$ and using the parabolic factorization $w=zy$ with $z\in W_J$, $y\in{}^JW$ and $1\otimes H_w=\varphi_-(H_z)n_y=(-v)^{\ell(z)}n_y$ gives $\Phi(\underline H_x)=\sum_{y\in{}^JW}\bigl(\sum_{z\in W_J}(-v)^{\ell(z)}p_{zy,x}\bigr)n_y$. The top coefficient at $y=x$ is $p_{x,x}=1$ (only $z=1$ contributes, since $zx\le x$ with $z\ne1$ would give $\ell(zx)>\ell(x)$); and for a coefficient at $y\ne x$, every contributing term has $zy\le x$, hence $y\le zy$ by [F5] and $y<x$. For $y<x$, every contributing ordinary coefficient has $zy<x$: equality $zy=x$ would contradict the unique parabolic factorization of the minimal representative $x$. Thus $p_{zy,x}\in v\mathbb Z[v]$, and multiplication by $(-v)^{\ell(z)}$ preserves this property. Hence $\Phi(\underline H_x)$ is bar-fixed in $n_x+\sum_{y<x}v\mathbb Z[v]n_y$, so by uniqueness [F4] it equals $D_x$ and matching coefficients gives (1).

**The integral parabolic eigenline.** Put $L=\ell(w_J)$ and $C_J=\sum_{u\in W_J}v^{L-\ell(u)}H_u$. Pairing $u$ with $su$ where $\ell(su)=\ell(u)+1$, the left multiplication rule gives $H_s(a_uH_u+a_{su}H_{su})=a_{su}H_u+(a_u+(v^{-1}-v)a_{su})H_{su}$. This equals $v^{-1}(a_uH_u+a_{su}H_{su})$ iff $a_{su}=v^{-1}a_u$. Iterating along reduced words proves that the simultaneous left eigenvectors in $H_J$ are exactly $A C_J$: their coefficients satisfy $a_u=v^{-\ell(u)}a_e=v^{L-\ell(u)}a_{w_J}$. The same pairing on the right gives $C_JH_s=v^{-1}C_J$. Bar preserves the left eigen-equations, since conjugating $H_sX=v^{-1}X$ gives $H_s^{-1}\overline X=v\overline X$ and hence $H_s\overline X=v^{-1}\overline X$. By [F1] its triangular standard expansion leaves the coefficient of $H_{w_J}$ in $\overline{C_J}$ equal to one. The integral eigenline calculation therefore forces $\overline{C_J}=C_J$. Every $u\in W_J$ is a reduced subword of a reduced expression for the block-reversing longest permutation $w_J$ (sort a block permutation up to the reverse order by adjacent ascents); thus $u\le w_J$. Consequently $C_J$ has the ordinary canonical triangular form, and [F1] identifies it with $\underline H_{w_J}$.

**Well-definedness and degree bounds for the antispherical family.** In the formula of step 1.1, a term with $p_{zy,x}\ne0$ has $zy\le x$ and $\ell(zy)=\ell(z)+\ell(y)$ by [F5], so $p_{zy,x}\in v^{\ell(x)-\ell(zy)}\mathbb Z[v^{-2}]$ by [F1]; multiplying by $(-v)^{\ell(z)}$ gives a contribution in $v^{\ell(x)-\ell(y)}\mathbb Z[v^{-2}]$. Hence $n_{y,x}\in v^{\ell(x)-\ell(y)}\mathbb Z[v^{-2}]$, so $N^J_{y,x}(q)=v^{\ell(y)-\ell(x)}n_{y,x}$ lies in $\mathbb Z[v^{-2}]=\mathbb Z[q]$ with $q=v^{-2}$, and $n_{y,x}$ has parity $\ell(x)-\ell(y)$ modulo two. This discharges the well-definedness of the antispherical polynomials.

**The integral spherical image.** Define $\Theta:M^J\to H_v(n)$ by $\Theta(1\otimes h)=C_Jh$. Step 1.2 proves balancing and bar compatibility. Decompose $H_v(n)=\bigoplus_{y\in{}^JW}H_JH_y$ as in [F3]. An element $X=\sum_yh_yH_y$ satisfies $H_sX=v^{-1}X$ for all $s\in J$ iff each $h_y$ does. The integral eigenline calculation of step 1.2 then gives $h_y=c_yC_J$ with $c_y\in A$. Thus the image of $\Theta$ is exactly this integral eigenmodule, and it is injective: the coefficient of $H_{w_Jy}$ in $C_JH_y=\sum_uv^{L-\ell(u)}H_{uy}$ is one, and no other coset contributes to that standard label. By [F2] in the descent case [F6], $\underline H_{w_Jx}$ lies in this image, with unique preimage $X_x=\sum_yc_ym_y$.

**Triangularity and coefficient comparison.** The disjoint coset expansions in step 2.2 give $c_y=p_{w_Jy,w_Jx}$. The coefficient $c_x$ is one. If $c_y\ne0$, then $w_Jy\le w_Jx$, so $y\le w_Jy\le w_Jx$. Choose a reduced expression for $w_Jx$ consisting of a word in $J$ followed by a reduced expression for $x$. By [F5] it contains a reduced subword for $y$. Such a subword cannot select any letter from the initial $J$-word: its first selected letter would be in $J$, making it a left descent of $y$, contrary to $y\in{}^JW$. Thus the subword lies entirely in $x$, proving $y\le x$. For $y\ne x$, the ordinary coefficient $p_{w_Jy,w_Jx}$ lies in $v\mathbb Z[v]$ by [F1]. Bar compatibility and injectivity give $\overline{X_x}=X_x$. Therefore $X_x$ has exactly the defining canonical form in [F4], so $X_x=C_x$ and $m_{y,x}=p_{w_Jy,w_Jx}$. This proves (2), including zero coefficients outside the lower ideal.

**Degree bounds and conclusion.** The ordinary degree bound of [F1] gives $p_{w_0^Jy,w_0^Jx}\in v^{\ell(x)-\ell(y)}\mathbb Z[v^{-2}]$, so $m_{y,x}$ has parity $\ell(x)-\ell(y)$ and $M^J_{y,x}(q)=v^{\ell(y)-\ell(x)}m_{y,x}\in\mathbb Z[q]$. Both families are therefore computable from the ordinary coefficients by (1) and (2), and both polynomial families are well defined.

boundaries.evidence: The sum over W_J in (1) is finite with z = 1 included; J = empty makes it the single term n_{y,x} = p_{y,x}, the empty-parabolic reduction recorded by the statement, so no empty sum occurs.
Antispherical coefficients may vanish: n_{e,s_2s_1} = p_{e,s_2s_1} - v p_{s_1,s_2s_1} = 0 in S_3, computed in the companion counterexample; no nonvanishing of lower coefficients is asserted.

Uniform top coefficients: p_{x,x} = 1 makes the single z-term give n_{x,x} = 1, and the spherical reduction gives m_{x,x} = p_{w_0^J x, w_0^J x} = 1. See the Statement and the numbered verification steps.

J = empty: W_J = {1}, so (1) is the identity n = p and (2) the ordinary reduction; J = S: ^JW = {e} and both formulas give the constant 1. The finiteness hypothesis on W_J in (2) holds throughout the page. See the Statement and the numbered verification steps.

The alternating sum is finite; its extremal term z = w_0^J is the endpoint of W_J and contributes (-1)^{ell(w_0^J)} v^{ell(w_0^J)} p_{w_0^J y, x}. See the Statement and the numbered verification steps.

boundaries.reason: Explicitly choice-free (final remark): the proof uses only the induced module structure, the ordinary basis theorem and uniqueness of bar-fixed triangular elements.
Both assertions (1) and (2) are equalities; the item states no biconditional.
There is no reverse implication to check; "computable with no separate recursion" is a corollary of the two displayed formulas.

reader_repair.description: Correct descent eigenvalue; integral coset eigenline; off-diagonal vZ[v] control and reduced-subword support before uniqueness.

risk_review.notes: The antispherical projection has top coefficient one and lower coefficients in vZ[v], since zy=x is excluded by unique factorization. The integral eigenline recurrence a_su=v^-1 a_u proves C_J spans the simultaneous eigenspace over A, and its top coefficient and bar invariance identify the ordinary longest canonical element. Disjoint cosets prove that Theta has the full integral image and is injective. A reduced subword for left-minimal y cannot begin in the initial J word, proving the preimage has support y<=x; ordinary positivity-in-v then permits canonical uniqueness. Both shifted families lie in Z[q] by the exact length-additive parity calculation. The empty/full parabolic cases and zero off-diagonal coefficients are covered. Libedinsky-Williamson section 2.7 supports both formulas; no AC.

citations.quote:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), inherited from the
published block theory. Work in category $\mathcal O$ of a finite-dimensional
complex semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$ with Cartan $\mathfrak h$,
positive system $\Phi^+$, simple roots $\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_r$, Weyl group
$W$, Weyl vector $\rho$ and dot action $w\cdot\lambda=w(\lambda+\rho)-\rho$, as
in [[def-bgg-category-o]] and
[[def-dot-action-facets-and-single-wall-translation-data]].

**(1) Dot-antidominant integral weights.** A weight $\mu$ is **dot-antidominant**
if $\langle\mu+\rho,\alpha^\vee\rangle\le0$ for every $\alpha\in\Phi^+$, and
**integral** if $\langle\mu,\alpha_i^\vee\rangle\in\mathbb Z$ for all $i$
([[def-integral-weyl-group-of-a-weight]],
[[def-integral-dominant-and-strictly-dominant-weights]]).

**(2) The dot stabilizer.** Fix such a weight $\mu$ and put
$$J=J(\mu):=\{i:\langle\mu+\rho,\alpha_i^\vee\rangle=0\},\qquad W_\mu:=W_J=\langle s_i:i\in J\rangle.$$
Then the dot stabilizer $\{v\in W:v\cdot\mu=\mu\}$ equals $W_J$. Indeed, for
$i\in J$ the reflection $s_i$ fixes $\mu+\rho$, so $W_J$ lies in the
stabilizer; conversely the stabilizer of an integral dot-antidominant weight
is generated by the reflections it contains and is a standard parabolic
([[lem-finite-weyl-closed-chambers-and-stabilizers]], applied to the dominant
vector $-\mu-\rho$), and by
[[def-cg-parabolic-quotient-and-two-sided-minima]] a standard parabolic
subgroup is $W_I$ for the set $I$ of simple reflections it contains, which is
exactly $J$. In particular $w'\cdot\mu=w\cdot\mu$ if and only if
$w^{-1}w'\in W_J$, that is, $w'\in wW_J$.

**(3) The singular integral block.** The **singular integral block**
$\mathcal O_\mu$ is the block of
[[thm-central-character-summands-split-into-linkage-blocks]] of the central
character $\chi_\mu$ of $\mu$; by
[[cor-central-characters-are-dot-weyl-orbits]] two central characters agree
exactly when the highest weights lie in one dot orbit, and by
[[thm-category-o-decomposes-by-generalized-central-character]] the block is a
summand of $\mathcal O$. Its simple objects $L(w\cdot\mu)$, standard objects
$\Delta(w\cdot\mu)=M(w\cdot\mu)$, costandard objects $\nabla(w\cdot\mu)$ and
projective covers $P(w\cdot\mu)$ are indexed by $w\in W$
([[def-standard-and-costandard-objects-in-category-o]],
[[def-verma-module]]); by (2) the label $w\cdot\mu$ depends only on the coset
$wW_J$, so the labels can be normalized by the minimal right coset
representatives

$$W^J=\{w\in W:\ell(ws)>\ell(w)\ \text{for all }s\in J\},$$

which are exactly the elements of minimal length in the cosets $wW_J$
([[thm-hh-parabolic-minimal-representatives-and-length-additivity]] (3));
inversion carries $W^J$ onto the minimal left coset representatives ${}^JW$,
and the two families are the label sets of the parabolic Hecke modules of
[[def-parabolic-hecke-module-and-antispherical-standard-basis]].

**(4) Highest-weight structure and multiplicities.** The block is a
highest-weight category: it has enough projectives
([[thm-category-o-has-enough-projectives]]), projective covers have finite
Verma flags ([[thm-projectives-in-category-o-have-verma-flags]]), the standard
classes and simple classes are bases of the Grothendieck group
([[def-grothendieck-group-and-character-of-category-o]],
[[prop-the-grothendieck-group-of-o-has-simple-and-standard-bases]]), and it
satisfies BGG reciprocity
$$(P(w\cdot\mu):\Delta(y\cdot\mu))=[M(y\cdot\mu):L(w\cdot\mu)]$$
([[thm-bgg-reciprocity]], [[def-verma-flag-and-its-multiplicities]]). The
multiplicity matrix is unitriangular for the refinement of the dominance order
on the dot orbit: $(P(w\cdot\mu):\Delta(w\cdot\mu))=1$, and
$(P(w\cdot\mu):\Delta(y\cdot\mu))\neq0$ only if $y\cdot\mu\ge w\cdot\mu$
([[cor-projective-standard-labels-lie-above-the-head]]); the ordinary
standard/costandard Hom and $\mathrm{Ext}^1$ vanishing used on this page is
[[lem-standard-costandard-hom-and-ext-vanishing]].

**(5) Regular versus singular.** The block is **regular** when $J=\varnothing$
(the weight lies on no wall) and **singular** when $J\neq\varnothing$; the
singular translation statements of this page use this notation, and
$J=\varnothing$ recovers the regular case. The genuine regular-parabolic
multiplicity statements below have their own separate explicit dominant
regular base and are not consequences of the notation here.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). For all weights
$\lambda$ and $\mu$,
$$(P(\lambda):\Delta(\mu))=[\Delta(\mu):L(\lambda)]=[M(\mu):L(\lambda)],$$
where $P(\lambda)$ is the projective cover of $L(\lambda)$, the left-hand
multiplicity is the Verma-flag multiplicity of
[[thm-projectives-in-category-o-have-verma-flags]], and the right-hand
multiplicity is the simple composition multiplicity of the Verma module
$M(\mu)$ ([[def-standard-and-costandard-objects-in-category-o]]).

Fix a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$, a Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak h$, and a positive Borel $\mathfrak b=\mathfrak h\oplus\mathfrak n^+$. Write $Q^+=\sum_i\mathbb Z_{\geq0}\alpha_i$, $\mu\leq\lambda$ when $\lambda-\mu\in Q^+$, and $w\cdot\lambda=w(\lambda+\rho)-\rho$.

For $\lambda\in\mathfrak h^*$, define the **standard** and **costandard** weight modules by

$$\Delta(\lambda)=M(\lambda),\qquad\nabla(\lambda)=D(M(\lambda)).$$

The Verma module is defined in [[def-verma-module]], and its restricted dual is defined in [[def-restricted-dual-of-a-weight-module]]. Under the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), [[prop-restricted-duality-is-an-exact-involution-on-category-o]] places $\nabla(\lambda)$ in $\mathcal O$, so both displayed modules are objects of that category. These symbols impose no projectivity or highest-weight-category axiom.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $(\lambda,\mu)$ be as
in [[lem-facet-tensor-weight-exclusion]]: $\lambda$ integral dot-antidominant
and dot-regular, $\mu$ integral dot-antidominant with $F_\mu$ in the closure
of the chamber $F_\lambda$, $J=J(\mu)$, $W_\mu=W_J$. Let $\nu$ be the unique
dominant weight of $W(\mu-\lambda)$ and let
$$T:=T_\lambda^\mu=\operatorname{pr}_{\chi_\mu}\circ(L(\nu)\otimes-)\circ\operatorname{incl}_{\chi_\lambda}\colon\mathcal O_\lambda\longrightarrow\mathcal O_\mu,\qquad T':=T_\mu^\lambda,$$
be the translation functors of [[def-translation-functor-between-o-blocks]],
which are exact and biadjoint
([[prop-translation-functors-are-exact-and-biadjoint-across-a-wall]]). Then:

**(1)** $T\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)\cong\Delta(w\cdot\mu)$ and
$T\nabla(w\cdot\lambda)\cong\nabla(w\cdot\mu)$ for every $w\in W$.

**(2)** $TL(w\cdot\lambda)\cong L(w\cdot\mu)$ if $w\in W^J$, and
$TL(w\cdot\lambda)=0$ otherwise; equivalently $TL(w\cdot\lambda)\neq0$ if and
only if $w$ lies in the set $W^J$ of minimal representatives of the cosets $wW_J$.

**(3) (Big projective on the wall.)** Let
$\Xi_\mu:=T_{-\rho}^{\mu}L(-\rho)$ be the translate of the simple object of
the most singular block. Then $\Xi_\mu$ is projective and injective in
$\mathcal O_\mu$, it is the projective cover $P(1\cdot\mu)$ of $L(\mu)$, and
$(\Xi_\mu:\Delta(w\cdot\mu))=1$ for every distinct orbit label (equivalently
for its representatives $w\in W^J$); consequently
$(P(\mu):\Delta(y\cdot\mu))=1$ for every distinct label $y\in W^J$ and
$[\Delta(w\cdot\mu):L(\mu)]=1$ for all $w\in W$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). For every
finite-dimensional $\mathfrak h$-semisimple $\mathfrak g$-module $E$ the
translation functor $T_{\chi,E,\chi'}$
([[def-translation-functor-between-o-blocks]]) is exact, and
$T_{\chi',E^*,\chi}$ is both a left and a right adjoint of
$T_{\chi,E,\chi'}$; in particular both functors send projectives to
projectives and injectives to injectives. Consequently, in the setting of
[[def-translation-functor-between-o-blocks]], $T_\mu^\lambda$ is both a left
and a right adjoint of $T_\lambda^\mu$, and the two functors are exact.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. In a regular integral type-$A$ block
$\mathcal O_\lambda$, for all $y,w\in W$
$$[M(y\cdot\lambda):L(w\cdot\lambda)]=(P(w\cdot\lambda):\Delta(y\cdot\lambda))=P_{y,w}(1),$$
with the pair ordered so that the multiplicity vanishes unless $y\le w$ in the
Bruhat order; in particular the Kazhdan–Lusztig conjecture's multiplicity
statement holds for every dominant regular integral weight, with the same
combinatorial answer.

Fix a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$ of type
$A_{n-1}$ with Cartan $\mathfrak h$, positive system $\Phi^+$, Weyl vector
$\rho$, Weyl group $W$ (identified with $S_n$) and dot action
$w\cdot\lambda=w(\lambda+\rho)-\rho$. Fix a dominant regular integral weight
$\lambda$, i.e. $\langle\lambda+\rho,\alpha^\vee\rangle\neq0$ for every root and
$\lambda$ integral, and let $\mathcal O_\lambda$ be the corresponding regular
integral block in the conventions of
[[def-regular-integral-category-o-block-and-its-antidominant-weight]]: standard
objects $\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)=M(w\cdot\lambda)$, simples $L(w\cdot\lambda)$,
indecomposable projectives $P(w\cdot\lambda)$ for $w\in W$, with
$\lambda=e\cdot\lambda$ the unique dominant and $w_0\cdot\lambda$ the unique
antidominant element and $\Delta(w_0\cdot\lambda)=L(w_0\cdot\lambda)$.

This item freezes the following conventions, each inherited from the cited
suppliers and used verbatim below.

(i) **Multiplicity conventions.** $(P(w\cdot\lambda):\Delta(y\cdot\lambda))$ is
the Verma-flag multiplicity of [[def-verma-flag-and-its-multiplicities]] and
$[M(y\cdot\lambda):L(w\cdot\lambda)]$ the composition multiplicity, and
$$(P(w\cdot\lambda):\Delta(y\cdot\lambda))=[M(y\cdot\lambda):L(w\cdot\lambda)]$$
by BGG reciprocity ([[thm-bgg-reciprocity]]).

(ii) **Bruhat reversal convention.** Along the bijection
$W\ni w\mapsto w\cdot\lambda$ the Bruhat order runs opposite to the dominance
order, in the two exact senses used on this page: $y\le w$ implies
$w\cdot\lambda\le y\cdot\lambda$ in the dominance order, and every nonzero
multiplicity forces the index direction, i.e.
$[M(y\cdot\lambda):L(w\cdot\lambda)]\neq0$ implies $y\le w$ in the Bruhat
order. The first sense is the inclusion direction of
[[lem-dominant-integral-dot-translates-embed-in-the-verma-module]] (for
$w\ge y$ one has $M(w\cdot\lambda)\subseteq M(y\cdot\lambda)$, so the highest
weight of the submodule is the lower one), and the second is
[[lem-jordan-holder-factors-of-verma-modules-lie-above-the-head]], which
confines every composition factor of $M(y\cdot\lambda)$ to labels
$w\ge y$. The full statement that the two orders are isomorphic as posets is
not needed here and is not asserted; only these two directions, together with
the finiteness of intervals of the Bruhat order
([[lem-bruhat-order-basic-properties-for-permutations]]), are used.

(iii) **Hecke and Kazhdan–Lusztig normalization.** The Kazhdan–Lusztig basis
$\underline H_w=\sum_{y\le w}p_{y,w}H_y$ of the normalized type-$A$ Hecke
algebra ([[thm-existence-and-uniqueness-of-the-kazhdan-lusztig-basis]]), with
$$p_{y,w}=v^{\ell(w)-\ell(y)}P_{y,w}(v^{-2})$$
in the classical $q=v^{-2}$ normalization
([[def-kazhdan-lusztig-polynomials-in-the-classical-q-normalization]]), support
$p_{y,w}=0$ unless $y\le w$, diagonal $p_{w,w}=1$, and simultaneous inversion
symmetry $p_{y^{-1},w^{-1}}=p_{y,w}$.

(iv) **Soergel label and character dictionary.** Write $R_x$ for the
polynomial standard graph bimodule supported at $x$, and $B_x$ for the
normalized indecomposable polynomial Soergel bimodule, which is generally not a
standard graph bimodule. With right reduction $\bar B=B\otimes_S\mathbb C$
and left coinvariant-module values of $V$, the projective dictionary is
$$V(P(w\cdot\lambda))\cong\bar B_{w^{-1}}$$
([[thm-indecomposable-projectives-correspond-to-indecomposable-soergel-modules]]).
The graph label $x$ corresponds to the standard
$\Delta(x^{-1}\cdot\lambda)$. The individual support ranks are measured on the
polynomial lift before reduction, as in
[[prop-verma-flag-multiplicities-are-standard-filtration-ranks-under-v]];
no separated graph-support filtration of the reduced module is asserted.

For degree bookkeeping use precisely the standard-generator normalization of
[[def-type-a-standard-graph-bimodules-support-filtrations-and-character]]:
$\Delta_x(d)=R_x(d-\ell(x))$, and $r_{x,d}(B)$ counts these normalized polynomial
standard layers. Thus the coefficient polynomial is
$$m_x(B;v):=\sum_d r_{x,d}(B)v^d,\qquad h_\Delta(B)=\sum_xm_x(B;v)\widetilde T_x,\qquad\widetilde T_x=v^{\ell(x)}T_x.$$
Here $\widetilde T_x$ is the normalized **standard** Hecke element $H_x$ used
in clause (iii) and
[[def-normalized-type-a-hecke-algebra-and-its-bar-involution]]. The published
Soergel split-Grothendieck-ring convention instead names its simple
Kazhdan--Lusztig generators $H_i=v(T_i+1)=\widetilde T_{s_i}+v$; these must not
be confused with the standard element $H_{s_i}=vT_i$
([[thm-split-grothendieck-group-of-the-soergel-category-is-the-type-a-hecke-algebra]]).
The standard-character supplier
[[lem-the-type-a-standard-character-is-multiplicative]] identifies $h_\Delta$
with that split-Grothendieck-ring isomorphism. This records the coefficient
normalization, and does not infer the image of a general indecomposable $B_x$
by multiplying simple generators. In particular the character theorem must be
used to identify $h_\Delta(B_x)$ with $\underline H_x$; a product of simple
Soergel classes is a Bott--Samelson class and need not be $[B_x]$.
The inverse labels and all rank comparisons above use auxiliary polynomial
gradings only; forgetting them gives the ordinary projective dictionary.

Identify $\mathbb Z[q]$ with $\mathbb Z[v^{-2}]$ by $q\mapsto v^{-2}$. For $y\le w$ in $S_n$, put $d=\ell(w)-\ell(y)$ and define the **Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomial** $P_{y,w}(q)\in\mathbb Z[q]$ by $$P_{y,w}(v^{-2})=v^{-d}p_{y,w},$$ where $\underline H_w=\sum_{y\le w}p_{y,w}H_y$ is the Kazhdan–Lusztig basis of [[lem-type-a-kazhdan-lusztig-basis-has-elementary-triangular-bar-properties]]. The parity clause of that theorem makes the right side a polynomial in $v^{-2}$. The conventions are: $P_{y,w}=0$ unless $y\le w$, $P_{w,w}=1$, $P_{y,w}$ has constant term 1, and for $y<w$ its degree is at most $(\ell(w)-\ell(y)-1)/2$. The **$\mu$-coefficient** is $$\mu(y,w):=	ext{coefficient of }q^{(\ell(w)-\ell(y)-1)/2}	ext{ in }P_{y,w},$$ defined to be 0 when $\ell(w)-\ell(y)$ is even; equivalently $\mu(y,w)$ is the coefficient of $v$ in $p_{y,w}$. One writes $\mu(y|w)
e0$ when $y
e w$ and ($y<w$ and $\mu(y,w)
e0$) or ($w<y$ and $\mu(w,y)
e0$). The dictionary with the literature is recorded for use: with the classical parameter $T_s^2=(q-1)T_s+q$ one has $H_w=v^{\ell(w)}T_w$, the element $\underline H_w$ is the basis element $C'_w$ of [EW], and $h_{y,w}=p_{y,w}$ with $v^{\ell(w)-\ell(y)}P_{y,w}(v^{-2})=h_{y,w}$ [EW, Remark 3.2].

For each $w\in S_n$ there is a unique element $\underline H_w\in H_v(n)$ with (i) $\overline{\underline H_w}=\underline H_w$ and (ii) $\underline H_w\in H_w+\sum_{y<w}v\mathbb Z[v]\,H_y$ (the sum over the lower Bruhat ideal of $w$). The elements $\{\underline H_w\}_{w\in S_n}$ form an $A$-basis of $H_v(n)$, and writing $\underline H_w=\sum_{y\le w}p_{y,w}H_y$ one has $p_{w,w}=1$, $p_{y,w}=0$ unless $y\le w$, $p_{y,w}\in v\mathbb Z[v]$ for $y<w$, the bar-duality $p_{x,w}=\sum_{y}r_{x,y}\,\overline{p_{y,w}}$ (matrix form $P=R\bar P$), and the symmetry $p_{y^{-1},w^{-1}}=p_{y,w}$. Moreover for $y<w$, with $d=\ell(w)-\ell(y)$: $p_{y,w}=v^{d}+\text{terms of strictly smaller degree}$ and $p_{y,w}\in v^{d}\,\mathbb Z[v^{-2}]$; in particular every $\underline H_w$ has integer nonnegative coefficients in the standard basis with $p_{y,w}$ of fixed parity $d\bmod 2$.

Let $n\ge1$ and $A:=\mathbb Z[v^{\pm1}]$. For $n\ge2$, define the **normalized type-A Hecke algebra** $H_v(n)$ to be the associative unital $A$-algebra presented by generators $H_{s_1},\ldots,H_{s_{n-1}}$ with relations
$$H_{s_i}^2=1+(v^{-1}-v)H_{s_i},\qquad H_{s_i}H_{s_{i+1}}H_{s_i}=H_{s_{i+1}}H_{s_i}H_{s_{i+1}},\qquad H_{s_i}H_{s_j}=H_{s_j}H_{s_i}\quad(|i-j|>1).$$
For $n=1$, set $H_v(1):=A$.

Here $S_n=\operatorname{Sym}(\{1,\ldots,n\})$, $s_i=(i\ i+1)$, and $\ell$ is inversion length as in [[def-symmetric-group]] and [[def-weyl-group-and-length-for-finite-gl-n]]. For $w\in S_n$, let $T_w$ be the standard basis element of the generic Hecke algebra of [[def-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]], formed from any reduced expression of $w$, and after the coefficient specialization $q\mapsto v^{-2}$ put $H_w:=v^{\ell(w)}T_w$. Equivalently, $H_w=H_{s_{i_1}}\cdots H_{s_{i_k}}$ for a reduced expression $w=s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_k}$. The standard-basis theorem [[thm-standard-basis-of-the-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]] and rescaling by units show that $\{H_w:w\in S_n\}$ is an $A$-basis of $H_v(n)$.

Right multiplication by a generator is
$$H_wH_{s_i}=H_{ws_i}\quad\text{if }\ell(ws_i)=\ell(w)+1,\qquad H_wH_{s_i}=H_{ws_i}+(v^{-1}-v)H_w\quad\text{if }\ell(ws_i)=\ell(w)-1.$$

**Dictionary with the generic normalization.** If the generic parameter in [[def-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]] is denoted by $q$, its relation is $T_i^2=(q-1)T_i+q$. The coefficient map $q\mapsto v^{-2}$ is the stated specialization, and $H_{s_i}=vT_i$. This gives $H_{s_i}^2=1+(v^{-1}-v)H_{s_i}$; the braid and commutation relations are unchanged. The two multiplication cases above are the standard-basis rule after the same rescaling.

**Bar assignment.** Let $F$ be the free associative $\mathbb Z[v^{\pm1}]$-algebra on the generator symbols. Define the semilinear algebra map $\iota_0:F\to F$ by $\iota_0(v)=v^{-1}$ and $\iota_0(H_{s_i})=H_{s_i}-(v^{-1}-v)$. In the quotient $H_v(n)$, the quadratic relation makes this latter element the two-sided inverse $H_{s_i}^{-1}$. The next lemma proves that $\iota_0$ preserves the defining ideal and descends to a well-defined involution $\iota$ on $H_v(n)$.

All items on this page use this normalization. It agrees with Elias–Williamson §3.2 under $H_x=v^{\ell(x)}T_x$ and $q=v^{-2}$.

Retain the notation of
[[def-parabolic-kazhdan-lusztig-basis-and-polynomials]].

**(1) (Antispherical alternating sum.)** For all $x,y\in{}^JW$,
$$n_{y,x}=\sum_{z\in W_J}(-1)^{\ell(z)}\,v^{\ell(z)}\,p_{zy,\,x},$$
the sum over all $z\in W_J$ (the product $zy$ taken in $S_n$, and $p_{\cdot,x}$
the ordinary coefficient of the Kazhdan--Lusztig basis of
[[thm-existence-and-uniqueness-of-the-kazhdan-lusztig-basis]], so the inner
coefficients vanish unless $zy\le x$).

**(2) (Spherical reduction.)** If $W_J$ is finite with longest element
$w_0^J$ then for all $x,y\in{}^JW$,
$$m_{y,x}=p_{w_0^Jy,\ w_0^Jx}.$$

In particular both families are computable from the ordinary Kazhdan--Lusztig
coefficients of $S_n$, with no separate recursion.

[[def-parabolic-hecke-module-and-antispherical-standard-basis]] and write the
parabolic Kazhdan--Lusztig bases of
[[thm-existence-and-uniqueness-of-the-parabolic-kazhdan-lusztig-basis]] as

$$C_x=\sum_{y\le x,\ y\in{}^JW}m_{y,x}\,m_y,\qquad D_x=\sum_{y\le x,\ y\in{}^JW}n_{y,x}\,n_y,\qquad x\in{}^JW,$$

with coefficients $m_{y,x},n_{y,x}\in\mathbb Z[v]$ supported on the lower
Bruhat ideal, $m_{x,x}=n_{x,x}=1$ and $m_{y,x},n_{y,x}\in v\mathbb Z[v]$ for
$y<x$.

The **spherical parabolic Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomials** are
$$M^J_{y,x}(q):=v^{-\ell(x)+\ell(y)}m_{y,x},\qquad q=v^{-2},$$
and the **antispherical (sign) parabolic Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomials** are
$$N^J_{y,x}(q):=v^{-\ell(x)+\ell(y)}n_{y,x}.$$

[[thm-parabolic-kazhdan-lusztig-polynomials-are-alternating-sums-of-ordinary-ones]]
make these polynomials in $q$; that reduction theorem discharges the
well-definedness asserted here and is recorded in `justified_by`. Values at
$v=1$ are written $m_{y,x}(1)$, $n_{y,x}(1)$.

antispherical family the $u=q$ normalization; the two are not related by a

longest element $w_0^J$, then

Let $(S,m)$ be a finite Coxeter matrix with presented group $W$, length $\ell$ and geometric representation $\sigma:W\to\mathrm{GL}_K(E)$ as in [[def-hh-coxeter-matrix-word-group-and-length]], [[def-hh-geometric-coxeter-representation-and-roots]] and [[lem-hh-dihedral-root-recurrence-and-root-sign]], and let $J\subseteq S$.

1. **Support and reduction.** For every $w\in W$ the set $S(w)$ of letters occurring in a reduced expression of $w$ is independent of the reduced expression, and every word in $S$ representing $w$ can be transformed into a reduced expression by repeatedly deleting two letters (Tits reduction, using only letters already present). Consequently
$$W_J=\langle J\rangle=\{w\in W:S(w)\subseteq J\}.$$
2. **Intrinsic parabolic presentation.** Let $W_J^\ast$ be the group presented by the restricted Coxeter matrix $(J,m|_J)$ in the sense of [[def-hh-coxeter-matrix-word-group-and-length]]. The canonical homomorphism $W_J^\ast\to W_J$, $s\mapsto s$, is an isomorphism. Hence $(W_J,J)$ is a Coxeter system, its intrinsic length function $\ell_J$ agrees with the ambient length $\ell$ on $W_J$, and $W_J\cap S=J$.
3. **Minimal coset representatives.** Every right coset $W_J a:=\{ua:u\in W_J\}$ ($a\in W$, [[def-coset]]) has a unique element $d$ of minimal length; it is characterized by $\ell(sd)>\ell(d)$ for all $s\in J$, and it satisfies
$$\ell(ud)=\ell(u)+\ell(d)\qquad\text{for all }u\in W_J .$$
Equivalently, every $w\in W$ has a unique factorization $w=u\,d$ with $u\in W_J$ and $d$ the minimal representative of the right coset $W_J d$, and then $\ell(w)=\ell(u)+\ell(d)$. By inversion ($w\mapsto w^{-1}$ preserves lengths and interchanges the two coset families $\{W_Ja\}$ and $\{aW_J\}$), every left coset $aW_J:=\{au:u\in W_J\}$ has a unique minimal element $d$, characterized by $\ell(ds)>\ell(d)$ for all $s\in J$ and satisfying $\ell(du)=\ell(d)+\ell(u)$ for all $u\in W_J$.
4. **Type A.** Let $n\ge2$, $S=\{s_1,\dots,s_{n-1}\}$ and $m(s_i,s_j):=3$ if $|i-j|=1$, $m(s_i,s_j):=2$ if $|i-j|>1$ (a Coxeter matrix of type $A_{n-1}$). Then $s_i\mapsto(i\ i+1)$ extends to an isomorphism $W\to S_n$ (the letters $1,\dots,n$ carry the library's symmetric group by the order-preserving identification with $\{0,\dots,n-1\}$, under which $(i\ i+1)$ is the adjacent transposition $(i-1\ i)$), and for every $w\in W$,
$$\ell(w)=\operatorname{inv}\bigl(\varphi(w)\bigr),$$
the inversion number of the corresponding permutation ([[def-inversions-inversion-number-and-sign]]). In particular a word in the $s_i$ is reduced if and only if its length equals the inversion number of its value.

derivations.claim: **Composition multiplicities on the wall.** Fix $y,w\in W^J$ and a composition series of $\Delta(y\cdot\lambda)$ with factors $L(z\cdot\lambda)$, $z\in W$. Exactness of $T$ [F2] turns it into a series of $T\Delta(y\cdot\lambda)\cong\Delta(y\cdot\mu)$ with factors $TL(z\cdot\lambda)$; by [F2] the only nonzero factors occur for $z\in W^J$, and then the factor is $L(z\cdot\mu)$, which can equal the simple $L(w\cdot\mu)$ only for $z=w$ since distinct $W^J$-labels have distinct dot translates [F1]. Hence $[\Delta(y\cdot\mu):L(w\cdot\mu)]=[\Delta(y\cdot\lambda):L(w\cdot\lambda)]$.

**Translate to the dominant base.** Let $\lambda_{\mathrm{dom}}:=w_0\cdot\lambda$; since $\lambda$ is dot-antidominant regular, $\lambda_{\mathrm{dom}}$ is dominant regular and $\lambda=w_0\cdot\lambda_{\mathrm{dom}}$, so for every $z\in W$, $z\cdot\lambda=(zw_0)\cdot\lambda_{\mathrm{dom}}$. Applying [F3] in the regular block of $\lambda_{\mathrm{dom}}$ gives $[\Delta(y\cdot\lambda):L(w\cdot\lambda)]=[M(yw_0\cdot\lambda_{\mathrm{dom}}):L(ww_0\cdot\lambda_{\mathrm{dom}})]=P_{yw_0,ww_0}(1)$, the ordinary value supported on $yw_0\le ww_0$.

**The spherical dictionary.** Conjugation by $w_0$ permutes the type-$A$ simple reflections, so the assignment $H_z\mapsto H_{w_0zw_0}$, $v\mapsto v$ is an algebra automorphism: it preserves the quadratic and braid presentations, the bar, length and Bruhat order. It sends a bar-fixed triangular element with top $H_b$ to one with top $H_{w_0bw_0}$; uniqueness in [F4] therefore gives $p_{a,b}=p_{w_0aw_0,w_0bw_0}$. Now set $k(w)=w_0^Jw^{-1}w_0$. Inversion sends $W^J$ to ${}^JW$ [F5]. In type $A$, left-minimality means that the values in each consecutive $J$-block occur in increasing order: the left descent $s_i$ occurs exactly when $i+1$ precedes $i$ in one-line notation. Right multiplication by $w_0$ reverses all positions, making those values decrease; left multiplication by $w_0^J$ reverses the values inside each block, restoring increasing order. Thus $k(w)\in{}^JW$. The spherical reduction [F5] gives $m_{k(y),k(w)}=p_{w_0^Jk(y),w_0^Jk(w)}=p_{y^{-1}w_0,w^{-1}w_0}=p_{w_0y,w_0w}=p_{yw_0,ww_0}$, using simultaneous inversion from [F4] and the conjugation symmetry just proved. Evaluating at $v=1$ and applying the classical normalization yields $m_{k(y),k(w)}(1)=P_{yw_0,ww_0}(1)$.
**The projective version.** By BGG reciprocity [F1], $(P(w\cdot\mu):\Delta(y\cdot\mu))=[M(y\cdot\mu):L(w\cdot\mu)]=P_{yw_0,ww_0}(1)$; this is the second displayed identity.

**Conclusion.** Combining the preceding steps, $[M(y\cdot\mu):L(w\cdot\mu)]=(P(w\cdot\mu):\Delta(y\cdot\mu))=P_{yw_0,ww_0}(1)=m_{k(y),k(w)}(1)$ for all $y,w\in W^J$, so the singular multiplicities are spherical parabolic values at one. The antispherical family is a different family (it is the sign-module normalization, used for the genuine regular parabolic category with dominant labels), and no change of positive system identifies the two; this is exactly the normalization distinction recorded in [[def-parabolic-kazhdan-lusztig-basis-and-polynomials]].

integral weight $\lambda$ of the complex type-$A$ Lie algebra and the standard
parabolic $\mathfrak p_J$, with reductive Levi $\mathfrak l_J$ and longest
Levi Weyl element $w_J$
([[def-standard-parabolic-and-levi-subalgebras-from-simple-roots]]). The
$\mathfrak p_J$-dominant weights in this regular block are exactly
$y\cdot\lambda$ for $y\in{}^JW$. Write
$\Delta^J(y\cdot\lambda)=M_{\mathfrak p}(y\cdot\lambda)$,
$L(x\cdot\lambda)$ and $P^J(x\cdot\lambda)$ for its generalized standards,
simples and projective covers
([[def-parabolic-category-o-for-a-standard-parabolic]]). Then for
$x,y\in{}^JW$,
$$[\Delta^J(y\cdot\lambda):L(x\cdot\lambda)]=(P^J(x\cdot\lambda):\Delta^J(y\cdot\lambda))=\sum_{u\in W_J}(-1)^{\ell(u)}P_{uy,x}(1)=n_{y,x}(1).$$

These are the antispherical sign coefficients, with support $y\le x$ and
diagonal $1$. The precise character/Grothendieck identity supplying the
formula is
$$\operatorname{ch}\Delta^J(y\cdot\lambda)=\sum_{u\in W_J}(-1)^{\ell(u)}\operatorname{ch}\Delta(uy\cdot\lambda).$$

$\lambda_{\mathrm{anti}}=w_0\cdot\lambda$, the actual longest-left label is
$z=yw_0$, since $y\cdot\lambda=z\cdot\lambda_{\mathrm{anti}}$.
Its shortest-left encoding is $a=\mathrm{lf}(y):=w_Jyw_0\in{}^JW$, so the
weight in that encoding is $(w_Ja)\cdot\lambda_{\mathrm{anti}}$, not
$a\cdot\lambda_{\mathrm{anti}}$. With $b=\mathrm{lf}(x)$, the reindexed matrix is
$$\widetilde N_{a,b}:=n_{\mathrm{lf}^{-1}(a),\mathrm{lf}^{-1}(b)}(1)=n_{w_Jaw_0,\,w_Jbw_0}(1).$$
It is the same multiplicity matrix with both indices permuted and has reversed
support in the transported order. It is not in general $n_{a,b}(1)$.
Every label retains its explicit dot-baseweight.
The highest-weight category theorem applies also to singular integral
parabolic blocks, but this ordinary regular KL matrix formula assumes the
ambient central character is regular. No singular/parabolic category
equivalence, grading or Koszul duality is asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let
$\mathfrak p=\mathfrak l_J\oplus\mathfrak u_J$ and $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$
be as in [[def-parabolic-category-o-for-a-standard-parabolic]]. Then:

**(1) (Simples.)** Within an integral block, $L(\lambda)\in\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$
if and only if $\lambda$ is $\mathfrak p$-dominant integral; every simple
object of $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ is of this form.

**(2) (Standards.)** For $\mathfrak p$-dominant integral $\lambda$ the
generalized Verma $M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$ lies in $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$,
has finite length, has $L(\lambda)$ as its unique simple quotient (head), and
$[M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda):L(\mu)]\neq0$ forces $\mu\le\lambda$ in the
dominance order; $M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$ is the largest quotient of
$M(\lambda)$ lying in $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$.

**(3) (Enough projectives.)** The inclusion
$\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}\subseteq\mathcal O$ is exact and has a left adjoint
$L_{\mathfrak p}$ (the largest $\mathfrak p$-locally-finite quotient);
$L_{\mathfrak p}$ is right exact and sends projective objects of $\mathcal O$
to projective objects of $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$. Consequently, for every
$\mathfrak p$-dominant integral $\lambda$ the object
$P^{\mathfrak p}(\lambda):=L_{\mathfrak p}(P^{(\mathcal O)}(\lambda))$ is a
projective cover of $L(\lambda)$ in $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$, and
$\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ has enough projectives and injectives.

**(4) (Generalized-standard flags, BGG reciprocity and duality.)** Every
projective in a fixed integral block has a finite generalized Verma flag. Its
projective cover surjects to its labelled generalized standard with a kernel
filtered by higher-labelled generalized standards. The simple and
generalized-standard classes form bases of the finite block Grothendieck
group, and characters are injective on this group. For $\mathfrak p$-dominant
integral $\lambda,\mu$,
$$(P^{\mathfrak p}(\lambda):M_{\mathfrak p}(\mu))=[M_{\mathfrak p}(\mu):L(\lambda)],$$
the multiplicities being finite; moreover restricted duality restricts to an
exact contravariant involution of $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ exchanging
$M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$ and $\nabla_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$, and
$\operatorname{Ext}^1_{\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}}(M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda),\nabla_{\mathfrak p}(\mu))=0$
for all $\lambda,\mu$.
