For $x,w\in S_n$ set $$q'_{x,w}:=\sum_{m\ge0}(-1)^m\sum_{x=z_0<z_1<\cdots<z_m=w}p_{z_0,z_1}p_{z_1,z_2}\cdots p_{z_{m-1},z_m}\in A,$$ where the inner sum is over strictly increasing Bruhat chains from $x$ to $w$, the $m=0$ chain occurs only when $x=w$, and $p_{u,v}$ are the coefficients of the Kazhdan–Lusztig basis ([[lem-type-a-kazhdan-lusztig-basis-has-elementary-triangular-bar-properties]]). Every chain lies in a finite Bruhat interval by [[lem-bruhat-order-basic-properties-for-permutations]], so the sum is finite. If $x\not\le w$ there are no chains; if $x=w$, the empty chain gives $q'_{w,w}=1$. If $x<w$, each chain has at least one factor $p_{u,v}\in v\mathbb Z[v]$ with $u<v$, so $q'_{x,w}\in v\mathbb Z[v]$.

Let $P=(p_{x,w})$ and $Q'=(q'_{x,w})$. The matrix $N:=P-I$ is strictly triangular on the finite Bruhat poset, hence nilpotent; the $(x,w)$ entry of $N^m$ is the sum of products over chains of $m$ strict steps. Therefore $$Q'=I-N+N^2-\cdots+(-1)^M N^M=(I+N)^{-1}=P^{-1},$$ where $M$ can be any integer at least the maximum strict-chain length. In particular, $Q'P=PQ'=I$ and $$\sum_zq'_{x,z}p_{z,w}=\delta_{x,w}=\sum_zp_{x,z}q'_{z,w}.$$

The **inverse Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials** in the classical sign convention are $q_{x,w}:=\mathrm{sgn}(x)\mathrm{sgn}(w)q'_{x,w}$. If $\Sigma$ is the diagonal matrix with entries $\Sigma_{x,x}=\mathrm{sgn}(x)$, then $Q=(q_{x,w})=\Sigma Q'\Sigma$. Equivalently, if $D_x$ is the basis of $H^*=\mathrm{Hom}_A(H,A)$ dual to the Kazhdan–Lusztig basis, then $$q'_{x,w}=D_x(H_w),$$ since $H_w=\sum_zq'_{z,w}\underline H_z$.

Let $P=(p_{x,w})$, $Q'=(q'_{x,w})$ and $R=(r_{x,y})$ be the triangular matrices of [[thm-existence-and-uniqueness-of-the-kazhdan-lusztig-basis]], [[def-inverse-kazhdan-lusztig-polynomials]] and [[thm-r-polynomial-recursion-and-degree-bounds]]. Then (a) $P=R\bar P$, $\bar P=\bar RP$, and $R\bar R=\bar RR=1$; (b) $Q'P=PQ'=1$, and the inversion formulas $$\overline{q'_{x,w}}=\sum_{x\le z\le w}q'_{x,z}r_{z,w},\qquad \overline{q_{x,w}}=\sum_{x\le z\le w}q_{x,z}\overline{r_{z,w}}$$ hold, i.e. $\bar Q'=Q'R$ and $\bar Q=Q\bar R$; (c) for the dual basis $D_x(\underline H_w)=\delta_{x,w}$ from [[def-inverse-kazhdan-lusztig-polynomials]], $D_x(H_w)=q'_{x,w}$. The inversion is proved from the bar-duality relations alone (no finite case check).

derivations.claim: **The matrix equation.** In the Grothendieck group write $M_y:=[\Delta^J(y\cdot\lambda)]$ and $L_x:=[L(x\cdot\lambda)]$; by [F1] and the Jordan-Holder theorem in the finite-length parabolic block, $M_y=\sum_x[\,\Delta^J(y\cdot\lambda):L(x\cdot\lambda)\,]L_x=\sum_{x\ge y}n_{y,x}(1)L_x$. Since the simple classes form a basis by [F2], this is the matrix equation $M=NL$ with $N=(n_{y,x}(1))$.

**Unitriangularity and inversion.** By [F1], $n_{x,x}(1)=1$ and $n_{y,x}(1)=0$ unless $y\le x$; the diagonal of $N$ is one and $U:=N-I$ is strictly upper triangular for the finite Bruhat-compatible order on ${}^JW$. Hence $U$ is nilpotent ($U^{m}=0$ for $m>\#{}^JW$) and $N^{-1}=I-U+U^2-\cdots$ is a finite sum of integer matrices; the $(x,y)$-entry of $N^{-1}$ is supported on $y\ge x$ and equals the finite signed chain sum $\sum_{m\ge0}(-1)^m\sum_{x=z_0<z_1<\cdots<z_m=y}\prod_{i}n_{z_i,z_{i+1}}(1)$ over strictly increasing chains. These are weighted incidence inverses of the finite poset, not generally ordinary Mobius values.

**The character formula.** Solving step 1.1 by step 1.2 gives $L=N^{-1}M$ with $N^{-1}$ read as a matrix whose rows are indexed by the simples and whose columns are indexed by the generalized standards, that is, $\operatorname{ch}L(x\cdot\lambda)=\sum_y(N^{-1})_{x,y}\operatorname{ch}\Delta^J(y\cdot\lambda)$; since $(N^{-1})_{x,y}$ is supported on $y\ge x$, this is exactly the displayed formula.

**Reindexing and conclusion.** Use $a=\mathrm{lf}(y)=w_Jyw_0$ as the shortest-left encoding of the actual longest-left label $yw_0$ in the antidominant base, so the same weight is $(w_Ja)\cdot\lambda_{\mathrm{anti}}$. The corrected dictionary in [[thm-parabolic-category-o-multiplicities-are-parabolic-kl-polynomials]] gives $\widetilde N_{a,b}=N_{\mathrm{lf}^{-1}(a),\mathrm{lf}^{-1}(b)}$. Reindexing both coordinates is conjugation by a permutation matrix, hence $\widetilde N^{-1}_{a,b}=N^{-1}_{\mathrm{lf}^{-1}(a),\mathrm{lf}^{-1}(b)}$; therefore $\operatorname{ch}L((w_Ja)\cdot\lambda_{\mathrm{anti}})=\sum_b\widetilde N^{-1}_{a,b}\operatorname{ch}\Delta^J((w_Jb)\cdot\lambda_{\mathrm{anti}})$, with the original support transported by $\mathrm{lf}$. Choosing the transported reversed order makes this matrix lower triangular. This preserves every character formula and constructs no Koszul or Ext grading.

Let $\le$ be the rank-inequality order on the zero-based $S_n$ of [[def-bruhat-order-on-the-symmetric-group]], and identify it with the one-based realization by shifting inputs and values by $1$. (a) This order is the strong Bruhat order of type A: the transitive closure of covers $x\to tx$ where $t$ is a transposition and $\ell(tx)=\ell(x)+1$. (b) If $y\le w$ then $\ell(y)\le\ell(w)$, with equality iff $y=w$; every saturated chain has $\ell(w)-\ell(y)$ steps; and $y\le w$ iff $y^{-1}\le w^{-1}$. (c) $y\le w$ iff for every reduced expression $w=s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_k}$, $y$ is a reduced subword. (d) For every simple reflection $s$, if $y\le w$ and $\ell(sy)>\ell(y)$, then $y\le sw$; if $y\le w$ and $\ell(sw)<\ell(w)$, then $sy\le w$. (e) Every interval $[y,w]$ is finite; if $y\le w$, then $[y,w]=\{y\}\cup\bigcup_{y\to a\le w}[a,w]$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). For all weights
$\lambda$ and $\mu$,
$$(P(\lambda):\Delta(\mu))=[\Delta(\mu):L(\lambda)]=[M(\mu):L(\lambda)],$$
where $P(\lambda)$ is the projective cover of $L(\lambda)$, the left-hand
multiplicity is the Verma-flag multiplicity of
[[thm-projectives-in-category-o-have-verma-flags]], and the right-hand
multiplicity is the simple composition multiplicity of the Verma module
$M(\mu)$ ([[def-standard-and-costandard-objects-in-category-o]]).

Multiplication gives a vector-space isomorphism

$$U(\mathfrak n^-)\xrightarrow{\sim}M(\lambda),\qquad u\longmapsto uv_\lambda.$$

Consequently, ordered negative-root PBW monomials from
[[thm-pbw-ordered-monomial-basis-for-the-enveloping-algebra]] applied to
$v_\lambda$ form a basis.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\alpha$ be a root of a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra
$\mathfrak g$ with respect to a Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak h$, with coroot
$h_\alpha$ as in [[def-coroot-of-a-lie-algebra-root]]. Then there are
$e_\alpha\in\mathfrak g_\alpha$ and $f_\alpha\in\mathfrak g_{-\alpha}$ with

$$[e_\alpha,f_\alpha]=h_\alpha,\qquad [h_\alpha,e_\alpha]=2e_\alpha,\qquad [h_\alpha,f_\alpha]=-2f_\alpha .$$

Consequently the span of $e_\alpha,f_\alpha,h_\alpha$ is a copy of
$\mathfrak{sl}_2$ inside $\mathfrak g$
([[def-special-linear-lie-algebra-sl-two]]).

Assume the Axiom of Choice.

If $\langle\lambda+\rho,\alpha^\vee\rangle<0$ for every $\alpha\in\Phi^+$, then $M(\lambda)$ is simple. Thus every regular antidominant weight, in this explicit sense, has simple Verma module.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), inherited from the
published block theory. Work in category $\mathcal O$ of a finite-dimensional
complex semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$ with Cartan $\mathfrak h$,
positive system $\Phi^+$, simple roots $\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_r$, Weyl group
$W$, Weyl vector $\rho$ and dot action $w\cdot\lambda=w(\lambda+\rho)-\rho$, as
in [[def-bgg-category-o]] and
[[def-dot-action-facets-and-single-wall-translation-data]].

**(1) Dot-antidominant integral weights.** A weight $\mu$ is **dot-antidominant**
if $\langle\mu+\rho,\alpha^\vee\rangle\le0$ for every $\alpha\in\Phi^+$, and
**integral** if $\langle\mu,\alpha_i^\vee\rangle\in\mathbb Z$ for all $i$
([[def-integral-weyl-group-of-a-weight]],
[[def-integral-dominant-and-strictly-dominant-weights]]).

**(2) The dot stabilizer.** Fix such a weight $\mu$ and put
$$J=J(\mu):=\{i:\langle\mu+\rho,\alpha_i^\vee\rangle=0\},\qquad W_\mu:=W_J=\langle s_i:i\in J\rangle.$$
Then the dot stabilizer $\{v\in W:v\cdot\mu=\mu\}$ equals $W_J$. Indeed, for
$i\in J$ the reflection $s_i$ fixes $\mu+\rho$, so $W_J$ lies in the
stabilizer; conversely the stabilizer of an integral dot-antidominant weight
is generated by the reflections it contains and is a standard parabolic
([[lem-finite-weyl-closed-chambers-and-stabilizers]], applied to the dominant
vector $-\mu-\rho$), and by
[[def-cg-parabolic-quotient-and-two-sided-minima]] a standard parabolic
subgroup is $W_I$ for the set $I$ of simple reflections it contains, which is
exactly $J$. In particular $w'\cdot\mu=w\cdot\mu$ if and only if
$w^{-1}w'\in W_J$, that is, $w'\in wW_J$.

**(3) The singular integral block.** The **singular integral block**
$\mathcal O_\mu$ is the block of
[[thm-central-character-summands-split-into-linkage-blocks]] of the central
character $\chi_\mu$ of $\mu$; by
[[cor-central-characters-are-dot-weyl-orbits]] two central characters agree
exactly when the highest weights lie in one dot orbit, and by
[[thm-category-o-decomposes-by-generalized-central-character]] the block is a
summand of $\mathcal O$. Its simple objects $L(w\cdot\mu)$, standard objects
$\Delta(w\cdot\mu)=M(w\cdot\mu)$, costandard objects $\nabla(w\cdot\mu)$ and
projective covers $P(w\cdot\mu)$ are indexed by $w\in W$
([[def-standard-and-costandard-objects-in-category-o]],
[[def-verma-module]]); by (2) the label $w\cdot\mu$ depends only on the coset
$wW_J$, so the labels can be normalized by the minimal right coset
representatives

$$W^J=\{w\in W:\ell(ws)>\ell(w)\ \text{for all }s\in J\},$$

which are exactly the elements of minimal length in the cosets $wW_J$
([[thm-hh-parabolic-minimal-representatives-and-length-additivity]] (3));
inversion carries $W^J$ onto the minimal left coset representatives ${}^JW$,
and the two families are the label sets of the parabolic Hecke modules of
[[def-parabolic-hecke-module-and-antispherical-standard-basis]].

**(4) Highest-weight structure and multiplicities.** The block is a
highest-weight category: it has enough projectives
([[thm-category-o-has-enough-projectives]]), projective covers have finite
Verma flags ([[thm-projectives-in-category-o-have-verma-flags]]), the standard
classes and simple classes are bases of the Grothendieck group
([[def-grothendieck-group-and-character-of-category-o]],
[[prop-the-grothendieck-group-of-o-has-simple-and-standard-bases]]), and it
satisfies BGG reciprocity
$$(P(w\cdot\mu):\Delta(y\cdot\mu))=[M(y\cdot\mu):L(w\cdot\mu)]$$
([[thm-bgg-reciprocity]], [[def-verma-flag-and-its-multiplicities]]). The
multiplicity matrix is unitriangular for the refinement of the dominance order
on the dot orbit: $(P(w\cdot\mu):\Delta(w\cdot\mu))=1$, and
$(P(w\cdot\mu):\Delta(y\cdot\mu))\neq0$ only if $y\cdot\mu\ge w\cdot\mu$
([[cor-projective-standard-labels-lie-above-the-head]]); the ordinary
standard/costandard Hom and $\mathrm{Ext}^1$ vanishing used on this page is
[[lem-standard-costandard-hom-and-ext-vanishing]].

**(5) Regular versus singular.** The block is **regular** when $J=\varnothing$
(the weight lies on no wall) and **singular** when $J\neq\varnothing$; the
singular translation statements of this page use this notation, and
$J=\varnothing$ recovers the regular case. The genuine regular-parabolic
multiplicity statements below have their own separate explicit dominant
regular base and are not consequences of the notation here.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix a finite-dimensional
complex semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$, a Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak h$,
and a positive Borel $\mathfrak b=\mathfrak h\oplus\mathfrak n^+$, with the
chosen positive system $\Phi^+$ and Weyl vector $\rho$ of
[[def-weyl-vector-rho-for-a-chosen-positive-system]] and Weyl group $W$ acting
by the root reflections
$s_\alpha(\lambda)=\lambda-\lambda(\alpha^\vee)\alpha$ of
[[def-root-reflections-and-the-weyl-group-action]]. Write the dot action as
$w\mathbin\cdot\lambda=w(\lambda+\rho)-\rho$ and write
$\langle\zeta,\alpha^\vee\rangle$ for the pairing with the coroot
([[thm-the-root-set-is-a-reduced-crystallographic-root-system]]).

Put $R=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb R}\Phi\subseteq\mathfrak h^*$. For a weight
$\lambda\in R$, the **dot-Weyl facet** of $\lambda$ is
the set of weights
$$F_\lambda=\{\zeta\in R:\ \operatorname{sgn}\langle\zeta+\rho,\alpha^\vee\rangle=\operatorname{sgn}\langle\lambda+\rho,\alpha^\vee\rangle\ \text{for every root }\alpha\in\Phi\},$$
where $\operatorname{sgn}$ takes the values positive, zero and negative. Its
**upper closure** is
$$F_\lambda^+=\{\zeta\in R:\ \langle\zeta+\rho,\alpha^\vee\rangle\ \text{is positive, zero or nonpositive according as}\ \langle\lambda+\rho,\alpha^\vee\rangle\ \text{is positive, zero or negative, for every }\alpha\in\Phi^+\}.$$
The upper-closure test uses only positive roots: imposing it also on their
negatives would incorrectly exclude wall points from the upper closure of
the antidominant chamber. Thus $F_\lambda\subseteq F_\lambda^+$, the facets refine the closures of the
open Weyl chambers, and $F_\lambda$ depends only on the wall-sign pattern of
$\lambda+\rho$.

Two special positions are used throughout. A weight $\lambda$ is **dot-regular**
when $\langle\lambda+\rho,\alpha^\vee\rangle\neq0$ for every root $\alpha$, so
that $F_\lambda$ is an open chamber; it is **dot-antidominant** when
$\langle\lambda+\rho,\alpha^\vee\rangle\le0$ for every positive root $\alpha$.
Integrality of weights is the notion of
[[def-integral-dominant-and-strictly-dominant-weights]].

A **single-wall translation datum** is a triple $(\lambda,\mu,\alpha)$
consisting of integral dot-antidominant weights $\lambda,\mu$ and a positive
root $\alpha$ such that:

1. $\lambda$ is dot-regular, so $F_\lambda$ is an open chamber;
2. $\mu+\rho$ lies in the closure of the chamber of $\lambda+\rho$: one has
   $\langle\mu+\rho,\alpha^\vee\rangle=0$, and
   $\langle\mu+\rho,\beta^\vee\rangle$ has the same sign as
   $\langle\lambda+\rho,\beta^\vee\rangle$ for every root $\beta$ different
   from $\alpha$ and from its multiples;
3. the dot stabilizer $S_\mu:=\{w\in W:w\mathbin\cdot\mu=\mu\}$ is exactly $\{1,s_\alpha\}$.

Equivalently, $F_\mu$ is a codimension-one facet in the closure of the open
antidominant chamber $F_\lambda$, with $S_\mu=\{1,s_\alpha\}$.
This dot stabilizer and the integral-reflection group $W_\mu$ of
[[def-integral-weyl-group-of-a-weight]] are defined by different conditions:
since $\mu$ is integral, all simple reflections belong to $W_\mu$, so
$W_\mu=W$, whereas $S_\mu=\{1,s_\alpha\}$. The groups coincide in rank one
and differ when the rank is greater than one. In
this datum the **translating weight** $\nu$ is the unique dominant weight of
the linear Weyl orbit $W(\mu-\lambda)$; it exists and is unique by
[[lem-finite-weyl-closed-chambers-and-stabilizers]], and it is integral because
$\mu-\lambda$ is integral and $W$ preserves the weight lattice. The **wall
reflection** is $s:=s_\alpha$.

The basic example is $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ with the datum
$(\lambda,\mu)=(-2,-1)$: here $\rho=1$, $\mu=-\rho$,
$\lambda+\rho=-1$ spans the open negative chamber, $\mu+\rho=0$ is the single
wall, and the dot-stabilizer of $\mu$ is $\{1,s\}$. The pair $(0,-1)$ uses the dominant regular representative rather than the
antidominant representative required here. It defines the same translation
functors: $0$ and $-2$ have the same central character, and both weight
differences have dominant representative $1$ with translating module
$L(1)$, which is self-dual. These functors are defined in
the next definition on this page.

derivations.claim: **The sl_2 singular block.** For $\mu=-1=-\rho$ the dot orbit is $\{-1\}$, so $\mathcal O_{-1}$ has the single simple $L(-1)$, and by [F2] $M(-1)=L(-1)=P(-1)=\nabla(-1)$ is projective and injective.
**The sl_2 translation.** Here $W^J=\{1\}$. By [F1], $TM(-2)=M(-1)$ and $TM(0)=M(-1)$; and on simples $TL(-2)=L(-1)$, while $TL(0)=0$ because $s\notin W^J$.

**The sl_3 matrices.** For $y=(1,s_2,s_1s_2)$ the products $yw_0=(w_0,s_1s_2,s_2)$ form the descending Bruhat chain $w_0>s_1s_2>s_2$ by reduced subwords. Their supported length gaps are zero, one or two. Thus [F3] gives the displayed LOWER unitriangular matrix $A$: its row $y$, column $w$ is one exactly when $y\ge w$. BGG [F4] gives the same entries for $(P(w\cdot\mu):\Delta(y\cdot\mu))$. Thus the column at $w=1$ consists of three ones, the column at $w=s_2$ has zeros at $y=1$ and ones at $y=s_2,s_1s_2$, and the column at $w=s_1s_2$ has only the diagonal one. These are precisely the corrected projective flags displayed above; reading rows gives the unchanged simple composition factors of the three Vermas.

**The sl_2 projective.** The relations in [F4] give $e f^kv_l=k(l-k+1)f^{k-1}v_l$ by induction using $[e,f]=h$ and $[h,f]=-2f$. For $l=0$, the span of $f^kv_0$, $k\ge1$, is the copy of $M(-2)$ generated by $fv_0$, and the quotient is the one-dimensional $L(0)$. Since $M(-2)$ is simple, BGG [F4] gives $(P(-2):\Delta(-2))=(P(-2):\Delta(0))=1$; the rank-one dot orbit has no further labels. Applying exact $T$ to this Verma flag gives two factors $\Delta(-1)=P(-1)$ by [F1] and step 1.1. Every extension of these projectives splits, so $TP(-2)\cong P(-1)\oplus P(-1)$.

**Surviving labels.** Applying [F1] to the simple labels: $L(w\cdot\lambda)$ survives translation iff $w\in W^J=\{1,s_2,s_1s_2\}$; hence $L(s_1\cdot\lambda)$ and $L(w_0\cdot\lambda)=L(s_1s_2s_1\cdot\lambda)$ are sent to zero, as are all other non-minimal labels. This proves every displayed assertion.

boundaries.evidence: For sl_2, W^J = {1} and the surviving label set is a singleton; for sl_3 the non-surviving labels s_1 and w_0 are explicitly listed as killed, so no case is left implicit. See the Example.

The zero outputs TL(0) = 0 (sl_2) and the killing of L(s_1 . lambda) and L(w_0 . lambda) (sl_3) are computed from the survival criterion; the singular block at mu = -1 = -rho has a single label and no vanishing multiplicities. See the Example.
Current step 2.1 gives TP(-2)=2P(-1); step 1.3 reads the lower sl3 matrix with entry1 iff y>=w and projective column vectors (1,1,1),(0,1,1),(0,0,1).

The sl_2 case mu = -1 = -rho is the most singular (degenerate) wall, where the single Verma is simple and P(-1) = M(-1) = L(-1); the sl_3 case retains a genuine singular block with three labels. See the Example.

The sl_2 facet list (-infinity,-1), {-1}, (-1,infinity) makes lambda = -2 and mu = -1 endpoint data of the wall; the minimal coset representatives W^J are the length endpoints of the cosets. See the Example.

boundaries.reason: The Axiom of Choice enters only through the quoted translation theorem and its suppliers; the computations are finite matrix readings that add no selection.

boundaries.evidence: The forward nonzero-implies-minimal direction is the contrapositive of the nonminimal killing examples in steps 1.2 and 3.1.
The reverse minimal-implies-nonzero direction is the survival of the rank-one identity label in step 1.2 and the three minimal sl3 labels in step 3.1.

reader_repair.description: Rank-one PBW/commutator sequence and BGG flag; valid singular citation; all used KL gaps at most two; explicit sl3 lambda.

risk_review.notes: The sl2 data (-2,-1) have full stabilizer and a single singular simple/projective. PBW and ef^k v=k(l-k+1)f^(k-1)v prove 0->M(-2)->M(0)->L(0)->0, so BGG gives the two P(-2) flag factors. Exact translation gives two projective P(-1) factors, and their extension splits. For sl3 lambda=-2rho is regular antidominant and mu+rho=-omega2 has stabilizer {1,s1}. The right minima are 1,s2,s1s2 and their products with w0 are w0,s1s2,s2. All needed ordinary gaps are at most two; the resulting lower all-ones matrix, its projective columns, and the stated weight differences were recomputed. Nonminimal s1 and w0 vanish. Inherited AC and zero functor images are explicit.

citations.quote:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix a dominant regular
integral weight $\lambda$ of the complex type-$A$ Lie algebra and the standard
parabolic $\mathfrak p_J$, with reductive Levi $\mathfrak l_J$ and longest
Levi Weyl element $w_J$
([[def-standard-parabolic-and-levi-subalgebras-from-simple-roots]]). The
$\mathfrak p_J$-dominant weights in this regular block are exactly
$y\cdot\lambda$ for $y\in{}^JW$. Write
$\Delta^J(y\cdot\lambda)=M_{\mathfrak p}(y\cdot\lambda)$,
$L(x\cdot\lambda)$ and $P^J(x\cdot\lambda)$ for its generalized standards,
simples and projective covers
([[def-parabolic-category-o-for-a-standard-parabolic]]). Then for
$x,y\in{}^JW$,
$$[\Delta^J(y\cdot\lambda):L(x\cdot\lambda)]=(P^J(x\cdot\lambda):\Delta^J(y\cdot\lambda))=\sum_{u\in W_J}(-1)^{\ell(u)}P_{uy,x}(1)=n_{y,x}(1).$$

These are the antispherical sign coefficients, with support $y\le x$ and
diagonal $1$. The precise character/Grothendieck identity supplying the
formula is
$$\operatorname{ch}\Delta^J(y\cdot\lambda)=\sum_{u\in W_J}(-1)^{\ell(u)}\operatorname{ch}\Delta(uy\cdot\lambda).$$

For the same highest weights in the antidominant base
$\lambda_{\mathrm{anti}}=w_0\cdot\lambda$, the actual longest-left label is
$z=yw_0$, since $y\cdot\lambda=z\cdot\lambda_{\mathrm{anti}}$.
Its shortest-left encoding is $a=\mathrm{lf}(y):=w_Jyw_0\in{}^JW$, so the
weight in that encoding is $(w_Ja)\cdot\lambda_{\mathrm{anti}}$, not
$a\cdot\lambda_{\mathrm{anti}}$. With $b=\mathrm{lf}(x)$, the reindexed matrix is
$$\widetilde N_{a,b}:=n_{\mathrm{lf}^{-1}(a),\mathrm{lf}^{-1}(b)}(1)=n_{w_Jaw_0,\,w_Jbw_0}(1).$$
It is the same multiplicity matrix with both indices permuted and has reversed
support in the transported order. It is not in general $n_{a,b}(1)$.
Every label retains its explicit dot-baseweight.
The highest-weight category theorem applies also to singular integral
parabolic blocks, but this ordinary regular KL matrix formula assumes the
ambient central character is regular. No singular/parabolic category
equivalence, grading or Koszul duality is asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and the dominant regular
integral conventions of
[[thm-parabolic-category-o-multiplicities-are-parabolic-kl-polynomials]]. Put
$N=(n_{y,x}(1))_{y,x\in{}^JW}$, with rows indexed by generalized standards and
columns by simples in a Bruhat-compatible order
([[def-parabolic-kazhdan-lusztig-basis-and-polynomials]]). Then $N$ is upper
unitriangular and, for each $x$,
$$\operatorname{ch}L(x\cdot\lambda)=\sum_{y\ge x}(N^{-1})_{x,y}\,\operatorname{ch}\Delta^J(y\cdot\lambda).$$
Its inverse entries are integers computed by the finite signed chain sum of
products of $n_{a,b}(1)$; they are weighted incidence inverses, not generally
ordinary Bruhat Mobius values. In the antidominant base $\lambda_{\mathrm{anti}}=w_0\cdot\lambda$, set
$a=\mathrm{lf}(y)=w_Jyw_0$ and encode the same weight as
$(w_Ja)\cdot\lambda_{\mathrm{anti}}$. The reindexed matrix is
$\widetilde N_{a,b}=N_{\mathrm{lf}^{-1}(a),\mathrm{lf}^{-1}(b)}$
and its inverse is reindexed by the same permutation; thus the same formula
has reversed support in the transported order. This does not replace the
entries by $n_{a,b}(1)$.
This is the ungraded
character formula for the regular parabolic block, and constructs no Koszul or
Ext grading.

Take $W=S_3$ with simple reflections $s_1,s_2$, let $J=\{s_1\}$, so
$W_J=\{1,s_1\}$ and the minimal left coset representatives are
${}^JW=\{e,\ s_2,\ s_2s_1\}$. In the notation of
[[def-parabolic-kazhdan-lusztig-basis-and-polynomials]] the two parabolic
families are computed from the ordinary Kazhdan--Lusztig coefficients of
$S_3$ (the ordinary coefficients needed below have length gap at most two and
are the monomials $v^{\ell(x)-\ell(y)}$): the **antispherical (sign)**
coefficients are

$$n_{e,e}=1,\quad n_{e,s_2}=v,\quad n_{e,s_2s_1}=0,\quad n_{s_2,s_2}=1,\quad n_{s_2,s_2s_1}=v,\quad n_{s_2s_1,s_2s_1}=1,$$

all other coefficients being zero; the **spherical** coefficients are

$$m_{e,e}=1,\quad m_{e,s_2}=v,\quad m_{e,s_2s_1}=v^{2},\quad m_{s_2,s_2}=1,\quad m_{s_2,s_2s_1}=v,\quad m_{s_2s_1,s_2s_1}=1,$$

all other coefficients being zero. At $v=1$ the antispherical matrix is
$\begin{pmatrix}1&1&0\\0&1&1\\0&0&1\end{pmatrix}$ and the spherical matrix is
$\begin{pmatrix}1&1&1\\0&1&1\\0&0&1\end{pmatrix}$ in the order
$(e,s_2,s_2s_1)$. The two families therefore already differ for this smallest
nontrivial parabolic: $n_{e,s_2s_1}=0$ while $m_{e,s_2s_1}=v^{2}$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and work in the type-$A$
root datum $W=S_n$ of the page's Hecke module and ordinary multiplicity
theorem. Let $(\lambda,\mu)$ be as in [[lem-facet-tensor-weight-exclusion]]
with $J=J(\mu)$, so $\mathcal O_\mu$ is the singular integral block of
[[def-singular-integral-category-o-block-and-stabilizer]] with labels
normalized by the minimal right coset representatives $W^J$, and let $w_0$ be
the longest element of $W$. Then for all $y,w\in W^J$,
$$[M(y\cdot\mu):L(w\cdot\mu)]=(P(w\cdot\mu):\Delta(y\cdot\mu))=P_{yw_0,\,ww_0}(1),$$
the value at $q=1$ of the ordinary Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomial attached to the
pair $(yw_0,ww_0)$ in the classical normalization of
[[def-kazhdan-lusztig-polynomials-in-the-classical-q-normalization]].
Equivalently, put $k(w)=w_0^Jw^{-1}w_0\in{}^JW$. Then
$$[M(y\cdot\mu):L(w\cdot\mu)]=m_{k(y),k(w)}(1).$$
This is the spherical family. The antispherical family instead governs the
genuine regular parabolic locally finite category with dominant labels;
changing to an opposite positive system does not identify the two families.
In particular all singular multiplicities are computable from the ordinary
Kazhdan--Lusztig coefficients of $S_n$, and no individual polynomial
coefficients beyond the value at one occur.

Let $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{sl}_2$ and use the coordinate
$l=\langle\lambda,\alpha^\vee\rangle$, so the dot action is $s\cdot l=-l-2$
and the facets are $(-\infty,-1)$, $\{-1\}$, $(-1,\infty)$
([[def-dot-action-facets-and-single-wall-translation-data]], Example 3.11 of
the source). Take $\lambda=-2$, $\mu=-1$. Then the singular block
$\mathcal O_{-1}$ has the single simple $L(-1)=M(-1)=P(-1)$, and the
translation functor $T=T_{-2}^{-1}$ satisfies $TM(-2)=M(-1)$, $TM(0)=M(-1)$,
$$TL(-2)=L(-1)\quad(\text{the label }1\in W^J),\qquad TL(0)=0\quad(\text{the label }s\notin W^J),$$
and $TP(-2)=2\,P(-1)$, because the projective cover $P(-2)$ of $L(-2)$ has
the Verma flag $\Delta(-2),\Delta(0)$ and both factors are sent to
$\Delta(-1)$.

For $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{sl}_3$ take $\lambda=-2\rho$, $J=\{s_1\}$ and the dot-antidominant
$\mu$ with $\mu+\rho=-\omega_2$; then $W^J=\{1,s_2,s_1s_2\}$ and by
[[thm-singular-category-o-multiplicities-are-parabolic-kl-polynomials]] the
composition and Verma-flag matrices of the singular block are
$$[M(y\cdot\mu):L(w\cdot\mu)]=(P(w\cdot\mu):\Delta(y\cdot\mu))=\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\1&1&0\\1&1&1\end{pmatrix}$$
in the row/column order $(1,\,s_2,\,s_1s_2)$: explicitly $M(\mu)$ is
irreducible, $M(s_2\cdot\mu)$ has composition factors $L(\mu),L(s_2\cdot\mu)$
once each, and $M(s_1s_2\cdot\mu)$ has all three simples once; dually
$(P(\mu):\Delta(y\cdot\mu))=1$ for all three $y$,
$(P(s_2\cdot\mu):\Delta(s_2\cdot\mu))=(P(s_2\cdot\mu):\Delta(s_1s_2\cdot\mu))=1$,
with its $\Delta(\mu)$ multiplicity zero, and
$P(s_1s_2\cdot\mu)=\Delta(s_1s_2\cdot\mu)$ has the single top-label standard.
The surviving
simple labels are exactly the minimal coset representatives, so translation
onto the wall kills $L(w\cdot\lambda)$ for $w\notin W^J$ (for instance
$L(s_1\cdot\lambda)$ and $L(w_0\cdot\lambda)$ in the $\mathfrak{sl}_3$ case).

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). For all weights
$\lambda$ and $\mu$,
$$(P(\lambda):\Delta(\mu))=[\Delta(\mu):L(\lambda)]=[M(\mu):L(\lambda)],$$
where $P(\lambda)$ is the projective cover of $L(\lambda)$, the left-hand
multiplicity is the Verma-flag multiplicity of
[[thm-projectives-in-category-o-have-verma-flags]], and the right-hand
multiplicity is the simple composition multiplicity of the Verma module
$M(\mu)$ ([[def-standard-and-costandard-objects-in-category-o]]).

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let
$\mathfrak p=\mathfrak l_J\oplus\mathfrak u_J$ and $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$
be as in [[def-parabolic-category-o-for-a-standard-parabolic]]. Then:

**(1) (Simples.)** Within an integral block, $L(\lambda)\in\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$
if and only if $\lambda$ is $\mathfrak p$-dominant integral; every simple
object of $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ is of this form.

**(2) (Standards.)** For $\mathfrak p$-dominant integral $\lambda$ the
generalized Verma $M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$ lies in $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$,
has finite length, has $L(\lambda)$ as its unique simple quotient (head), and
$[M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda):L(\mu)]\neq0$ forces $\mu\le\lambda$ in the
dominance order; $M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$ is the largest quotient of
$M(\lambda)$ lying in $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$.

**(3) (Enough projectives.)** The inclusion
$\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}\subseteq\mathcal O$ is exact and has a left adjoint
$L_{\mathfrak p}$ (the largest $\mathfrak p$-locally-finite quotient);
$L_{\mathfrak p}$ is right exact and sends projective objects of $\mathcal O$
to projective objects of $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$. Consequently, for every
$\mathfrak p$-dominant integral $\lambda$ the object
$P^{\mathfrak p}(\lambda):=L_{\mathfrak p}(P^{(\mathcal O)}(\lambda))$ is a
projective cover of $L(\lambda)$ in $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$, and
$\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ has enough projectives and injectives.

**(4) (Generalized-standard flags, BGG reciprocity and duality.)** Every
projective in a fixed integral block has a finite generalized Verma flag. Its
projective cover surjects to its labelled generalized standard with a kernel
filtered by higher-labelled generalized standards. The simple and
generalized-standard classes form bases of the finite block Grothendieck
group, and characters are injective on this group. For $\mathfrak p$-dominant
integral $\lambda,\mu$,
$$(P^{\mathfrak p}(\lambda):M_{\mathfrak p}(\mu))=[M_{\mathfrak p}(\mu):L(\lambda)],$$
the multiplicities being finite; moreover restricted duality restricts to an
exact contravariant involution of $\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}$ exchanging
$M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$ and $\nabla_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda)$, and
$\operatorname{Ext}^1_{\mathcal O^{\mathfrak p}}(M_{\mathfrak p}(\lambda),\nabla_{\mathfrak p}(\mu))=0$
for all $\lambda,\mu$.

Fix a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$, a Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak h$, and a positive Borel $\mathfrak b=\mathfrak h\oplus\mathfrak n^+$. Write $Q^+=\sum_i\mathbb Z_{\geq0}\alpha_i$, $\mu\leq\lambda$ when $\lambda-\mu\in Q^+$, and $w\cdot\lambda=w(\lambda+\rho)-\rho$.

For the abelian category [[thm-category-o-is-abelian-and-extension-closed]], define $K_0(\mathcal O)$ as the free abelian group on isomorphism classes $[M]$, modulo $[B]=[A]+[C]$ for every short exact sequence $0\to A\to B\to C\to0$. A set of representatives suffices: every finitely generated $U(\mathfrak g)$-module is a quotient of some $U(\mathfrak g)^n$, and those quotients form a set up to isomorphism.

Define the formal character by $\operatorname{ch}M=\sum_\mu(\dim M_\mu)e^\mu$. By [[prop-equivalent-support-description-of-category-o]], its integer coefficients are finite and supported in finitely many downward cones. Let $\mathscr R$ be the group of all such integer coefficient families, with pointwise addition. It is a ring with $e^\mu e^\nu=e^{\mu+\nu}$: at a fixed resulting weight, in any pair of cones the equation $\beta+\gamma=\eta$ with $\beta,\gamma\in Q^+$ has finitely many solutions, since every simple-root coefficient is bounded. Taking weight spaces is exact, so character gives a well-defined homomorphism $K_0(\mathcal O)\to\mathscr R$. The zero object's class and character are zero.

Assume the Axiom of Choice.

Fix a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$, a Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak h$, and a positive Borel $\mathfrak b=\mathfrak h\oplus\mathfrak n^+$. Write $Q^+=\sum_i\mathbb Z_{\geq0}\alpha_i$, $\mu\leq\lambda$ when $\lambda-\mu\in Q^+$, and $w\cdot\lambda=w(\lambda+\rho)-\rho$.

The classes $[L(\lambda)]$, and separately the classes $[M(\lambda)]$, form $\mathbb Z$-bases of $K_0(\mathcal O)$. For a fixed finite central-character label set $\Lambda=W\cdot\lambda$, the transition between its standard and simple classes is unitriangular in any linear order extending $\leq$. This remains true on a downward-closed subset of that finite poset. It is not a claim about finite downward ideals of all of $\mathfrak h^*$.

For $x,w\in S_n$ set $$q'_{x,w}:=\sum_{m\ge0}(-1)^m\sum_{x=z_0<z_1<\cdots<z_m=w}p_{z_0,z_1}p_{z_1,z_2}\cdots p_{z_{m-1},z_m}\in A,$$ where the inner sum is over strictly increasing Bruhat chains from $x$ to $w$, the $m=0$ chain occurs only when $x=w$, and $p_{u,v}$ are the coefficients of the Kazhdan–Lusztig basis ([[lem-type-a-kazhdan-lusztig-basis-has-elementary-triangular-bar-properties]]). Every chain lies in a finite Bruhat interval by [[lem-bruhat-order-basic-properties-for-permutations]], so the sum is finite. If $x\not\le w$ there are no chains; if $x=w$, the empty chain gives $q'_{w,w}=1$. If $x<w$, each chain has at least one factor $p_{u,v}\in v\mathbb Z[v]$ with $u<v$, so $q'_{x,w}\in v\mathbb Z[v]$.

Let $P=(p_{x,w})$ and $Q'=(q'_{x,w})$. The matrix $N:=P-I$ is strictly triangular on the finite Bruhat poset, hence nilpotent; the $(x,w)$ entry of $N^m$ is the sum of products over chains of $m$ strict steps. Therefore $$Q'=I-N+N^2-\cdots+(-1)^M N^M=(I+N)^{-1}=P^{-1},$$ where $M$ can be any integer at least the maximum strict-chain length. In particular, $Q'P=PQ'=I$ and $$\sum_zq'_{x,z}p_{z,w}=\delta_{x,w}=\sum_zp_{x,z}q'_{z,w}.$$

The **inverse Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials** in the classical sign convention are $q_{x,w}:=\mathrm{sgn}(x)\mathrm{sgn}(w)q'_{x,w}$. If $\Sigma$ is the diagonal matrix with entries $\Sigma_{x,x}=\mathrm{sgn}(x)$, then $Q=(q_{x,w})=\Sigma Q'\Sigma$. Equivalently, if $D_x$ is the basis of $H^*=\mathrm{Hom}_A(H,A)$ dual to the Kazhdan–Lusztig basis, then $$q'_{x,w}=D_x(H_w),$$ since $H_w=\sum_zq'_{z,w}\underline H_z$.

Let $P=(p_{x,w})$, $Q'=(q'_{x,w})$ and $R=(r_{x,y})$ be the triangular matrices of [[thm-existence-and-uniqueness-of-the-kazhdan-lusztig-basis]], [[def-inverse-kazhdan-lusztig-polynomials]] and [[thm-r-polynomial-recursion-and-degree-bounds]]. Then (a) $P=R\bar P$, $\bar P=\bar RP$, and $R\bar R=\bar RR=1$; (b) $Q'P=PQ'=1$, and the inversion formulas $$\overline{q'_{x,w}}=\sum_{x\le z\le w}q'_{x,z}r_{z,w},\qquad \overline{q_{x,w}}=\sum_{x\le z\le w}q_{x,z}\overline{r_{z,w}}$$ hold, i.e. $\bar Q'=Q'R$ and $\bar Q=Q\bar R$; (c) for the dual basis $D_x(\underline H_w)=\delta_{x,w}$ from [[def-inverse-kazhdan-lusztig-polynomials]], $D_x(H_w)=q'_{x,w}$. The inversion is proved from the bar-duality relations alone (no finite case check).

Let $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{sl}_2$ and use the coordinate
$l=\langle\lambda,\alpha^\vee\rangle$, so the dot action is $s\cdot l=-l-2$
and the facets are $(-\infty,-1)$, $\{-1\}$, $(-1,\infty)$
([[def-dot-action-facets-and-single-wall-translation-data]], Example 3.11 of
the source). Take $\lambda=-2$, $\mu=-1$. Then the singular block
$\mathcal O_{-1}$ has the single simple $L(-1)=M(-1)=P(-1)$, and the
translation functor $T=T_{-2}^{-1}$ satisfies $TM(-2)=M(-1)$, $TM(0)=M(-1)$,
$$TL(-2)=L(-1)\quad(\text{the label }1\in W^J),\qquad TL(0)=0\quad(\text{the label }s\notin W^J),$$
and $TP(-2)=2\,P(-1)$, because the projective cover $P(-2)$ of $L(-2)$ has
the Verma flag $\Delta(-2),\Delta(0)$ and both factors are sent to
$\Delta(-1)$.

For $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{sl}_3$ take $\lambda=-2\rho$, $J=\{s_1\}$ and the dot-antidominant
$\mu$ with $\mu+\rho=-\omega_2$; then $W^J=\{1,s_2,s_1s_2\}$ and by
[[thm-singular-category-o-multiplicities-are-parabolic-kl-polynomials]] the
composition and Verma-flag matrices of the singular block are
$$[M(y\cdot\mu):L(w\cdot\mu)]=(P(w\cdot\mu):\Delta(y\cdot\mu))=\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\1&1&0\\1&1&1\end{pmatrix}$$
in the row/column order $(1,\,s_2,\,s_1s_2)$: explicitly $M(\mu)$ is
irreducible, $M(s_2\cdot\mu)$ has composition factors $L(\mu),L(s_2\cdot\mu)$
once each, and $M(s_1s_2\cdot\mu)$ has all three simples once; dually
$(P(\mu):\Delta(y\cdot\mu))=1$ for all three $y$,
$(P(s_2\cdot\mu):\Delta(s_2\cdot\mu))=(P(s_2\cdot\mu):\Delta(s_1s_2\cdot\mu))=1$,
with its $\Delta(\mu)$ multiplicity zero, and
$P(s_1s_2\cdot\mu)=\Delta(s_1s_2\cdot\mu)$ has the single top-label standard.
The surviving
simple labels are exactly the minimal coset representatives, so translation
onto the wall kills $L(w\cdot\lambda)$ for $w\notin W^J$ (for instance
$L(s_1\cdot\lambda)$ and $L(w_0\cdot\lambda)$ in the $\mathfrak{sl}_3$ case).

derivations.claim: **The parabolic matrix.** By [F2] the matrix $N=(n_{y,x}(1))$ in the order $(e,s_2,s_2s_1)$ is the displayed upper unitriangular matrix. The displayed matrix $N^{-1}$ is its inverse: $N N^{-1}$ has entries $\sum_z n_{y,z}(1)(N^{-1})_{z,x}$, which equal $1$ for $y=x$ and $0$ otherwise (the only nonzero contributions are from $z\in\{y,\ldots,x\}$ with the alternating coefficients), and similarly $N^{-1}N=I$. Both products are finite integer calculations.

**The singular matrix.** By [F3] the composition matrix in the order $(e,s_2,s_1s_2)$ is $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\1&1&0\\1&1&1\end{pmatrix}$ (entry $(y,w)$ is $1$ exactly when $y\ge w$). The displayed matrix $B=\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\-1&1&0\\0&-1&1\end{pmatrix}$ satisfies $AB=I=BA$ by the same finite chain computation, so $A^{-1}=B$.

**The parabolic characters.** By [F1] and step 1.1, $\operatorname{ch}L(x\cdot\lambda)=\sum_y(N^{-1})_{x,y}\operatorname{ch}\Delta^J(y\cdot\lambda)$. Reading the rows of $N^{-1}$ in the order $(e,s_2,s_2s_1)$ gives exactly the three displayed character identities, using $0$, $-\alpha_2$, $-\alpha_1-2\alpha_2$ as the labels of $e\cdot0$, $s_2\cdot0$, $s_2s_1\cdot0$ by [F5]: with $\rho=\alpha_1+\alpha_2$, the type-$A_2$ reflection relations give $s_2\rho=\alpha_1$ and $s_2s_1\rho=-\alpha_2$, hence the stated dot translates after subtracting $\rho$.

**The singular characters and the comparison.** By [F3] and [F4], $\operatorname{ch}L(w\cdot\mu)=\sum_y(A^{-1})_{w,y}\operatorname{ch}M(y\cdot\mu)$; the rows of $B=A^{-1}$ give the three displayed singular identities, in which the nonzero off-diagonal coefficients are the Mobius values $\pm1$ of this all-one chain only. The parabolic coefficients of step 2.1 include the value $+1$ in the $(1,3)$ position of $N^{-1}$, which the singular inverse does not have: the two formulas are different character formulas for different blocks, and the singular one is not the generalized-Verma character formula of the parabolic category.

boundaries.evidence: The two displayed label sets each have three elements, so no index is omitted. The empty chain gives the inverse diagonal entries; the complete inverse matrices are verified in steps 1.1–1.2.

The zero comparison is the point of the example: the parabolic inverse has +1 in the (1,3) position while the singular inverse has 0 there; all zero entries of the displayed matrices are in the recorded positions.
Both N and B = A^{-1} have diagonal one, and the two matrix products are checked entrywise in steps 1.1 and 1.2.

The example is the smallest case with a nontrivial parabolic (S_3, J = {s_1}) and keeps the two label orders (left- versus right-minimal representatives) distinct; no degenerate identification of the two blocks is used.

The weights 0 and -alpha1-2alpha2 are the endpoints of the allowed three-label parabolic chain, not the endpoints of the full regular dot orbit. The singular chain has the three explicit labels at mu+rho=-omega2. See the Example and step 2.1.
The Axiom of Choice is declared and inherited from the multiplicity and inversion suppliers; the example adds only finite integer matrix computations.

boundaries.reason: The example asserts no biconditional; the comparison is a difference statement witnessed by one matrix entry.
No converse direction exists; the conclusion that the singular example is not the generalized-Verma character formula of the parabolic category is one-directional.

reader_repair.description: Parabolic basis supplier for generalized standards and explicit regular dot-weight computation.

risk_review.notes: All four integer products N*N^-1=N^-1*N=A*B=B*A=I were recomputed, with N upper bidiagonal and A the lower all-ones chain. The generalized-standard basis is supplied by the parabolic highest-weight theorem rather than the ordinary Verma basis. The explicit rho=alpha1+alpha2 reflections give weights 0,-alpha2,-alpha1-2alpha2; reading the inverse rows produces precisely the displayed three parabolic characters. The singular inverse gives M(mu), M(s2.mu)-M(mu), M(s1s2.mu)-M(s2.mu). Only the all-ones singular matrix is a zeta incidence matrix, so its Mobius comparison is correctly limited to that chain. The +1 corner of the parabolic inverse differs from the singular zero. No singular/parabolic equivalence or grading is asserted; AC is inherited.

Assume inherited AC [[def-axiom-of-choice]] for the invoked based/global lattice suppliers.

Work in the conventions of
[[def-higher-level-wedge-tensor-fock-module]] and
[[def-the-fock-convention-dictionary-for-finite-type-a-quantum-modules]], with
source parameter $s$ and the ordered column-monomial basis
$\{M_A:A\in\mathrm{Col}^\Lambda\}$ of
[[thm-higher-level-wedge-tensor-fock-module-has-the-column-monomial-basis]].

(1) On every finite interval the Fock module carries an **ordinary compatible
bar** $\psi$, the tensor-product quasi-$R$ bar built from the factors' own
normalized bars on the finite-product based integrable modules of
[[thm-quasi-r-tensor-bars-on-finite-products-of-based-integrable-modules]].
It is involutive (semilinear with $s\mapsto s^{-1}$) and independent of the
parenthesization of the tensor factors.

(2) It is **triangular** on the monomial basis:
$$\psi M_A=M_A+\sum_{B<A}\mathbb Z[s^{\pm1}]\,M_B$$
in the Bruhat order of the Definition; it fixes each ordered fundamental wedge,
and it preserves the integral monomial lattice
$\bigoplus_A\mathbb Z[s^{\pm1}]M_A$.

(3) Both kinds of truncation commute with $\psi$ and preserve the actual
charts and bases: an upper-cut inclusion of the smaller coordinate alphabet (equivalently the inverse identification on the supported truncation),
and the common-bottom-tail embedding
$\iota_k(M_A)=M_{A\sqcup(k-1)^l}$, satisfy

including the semi-infinite columns.

Its finite products are used only on actual finite-Cartan based fundamental
factors; no universal two-sided-unbounded tensor theorem and no arbitrary
integral quasi-$R$ action claim is imported.

Let $n\ge1$ and $A:=\mathbb Z[v^{\pm1}]$. For $n\ge2$, define the **normalized type-A Hecke algebra** $H_v(n)$ to be the associative unital $A$-algebra presented by generators $H_{s_1},\ldots,H_{s_{n-1}}$ with relations
$$H_{s_i}^2=1+(v^{-1}-v)H_{s_i},\qquad H_{s_i}H_{s_{i+1}}H_{s_i}=H_{s_{i+1}}H_{s_i}H_{s_{i+1}},\qquad H_{s_i}H_{s_j}=H_{s_j}H_{s_i}\quad(|i-j|>1).$$
For $n=1$, set $H_v(1):=A$.

Here $S_n=\operatorname{Sym}(\{1,\ldots,n\})$, $s_i=(i\ i+1)$, and $\ell$ is inversion length as in [[def-symmetric-group]] and [[def-weyl-group-and-length-for-finite-gl-n]]. For $w\in S_n$, let $T_w$ be the standard basis element of the generic Hecke algebra of [[def-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]], formed from any reduced expression of $w$, and after the coefficient specialization $q\mapsto v^{-2}$ put $H_w:=v^{\ell(w)}T_w$. Equivalently, $H_w=H_{s_{i_1}}\cdots H_{s_{i_k}}$ for a reduced expression $w=s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_k}$. The standard-basis theorem [[thm-standard-basis-of-the-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]] and rescaling by units show that $\{H_w:w\in S_n\}$ is an $A$-basis of $H_v(n)$.

Right multiplication by a generator is
$$H_wH_{s_i}=H_{ws_i}\quad\text{if }\ell(ws_i)=\ell(w)+1,\qquad H_wH_{s_i}=H_{ws_i}+(v^{-1}-v)H_w\quad\text{if }\ell(ws_i)=\ell(w)-1.$$

**Dictionary with the generic normalization.** If the generic parameter in [[def-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]] is denoted by $q$, its relation is $T_i^2=(q-1)T_i+q$. The coefficient map $q\mapsto v^{-2}$ is the stated specialization, and $H_{s_i}=vT_i$. This gives $H_{s_i}^2=1+(v^{-1}-v)H_{s_i}$; the braid and commutation relations are unchanged. The two multiplication cases above are the standard-basis rule after the same rescaling.

**Bar assignment.** Let $F$ be the free associative $\mathbb Z[v^{\pm1}]$-algebra on the generator symbols. Define the semilinear algebra map $\iota_0:F\to F$ by $\iota_0(v)=v^{-1}$ and $\iota_0(H_{s_i})=H_{s_i}-(v^{-1}-v)$. In the quotient $H_v(n)$, the quadratic relation makes this latter element the two-sided inverse $H_{s_i}^{-1}$. The next lemma proves that $\iota_0$ preserves the defining ideal and descends to a well-defined involution $\iota$ on $H_v(n)$.

All items on this page use this normalization. It agrees with Elias–Williamson §3.2 under $H_x=v^{\ell(x)}T_x$ and $q=v^{-2}$.

For each $w\in S_n$ there is a unique element $\underline H_w\in H_v(n)$ with (i) $\overline{\underline H_w}=\underline H_w$ and (ii) $\underline H_w\in H_w+\sum_{y<w}v\mathbb Z[v]\,H_y$ (the sum over the lower Bruhat ideal of $w$). The elements $\{\underline H_w\}_{w\in S_n}$ form an $A$-basis of $H_v(n)$, and writing $\underline H_w=\sum_{y\le w}p_{y,w}H_y$ one has $p_{w,w}=1$, $p_{y,w}=0$ unless $y\le w$, $p_{y,w}\in v\mathbb Z[v]$ for $y<w$, the bar-duality $p_{x,w}=\sum_{y}r_{x,y}\,\overline{p_{y,w}}$ (matrix form $P=R\bar P$), and the symmetry $p_{y^{-1},w^{-1}}=p_{y,w}$. Moreover for $y<w$, with $d=\ell(w)-\ell(y)$: $p_{y,w}=v^{d}+\text{terms of strictly smaller degree}$ and $p_{y,w}\in v^{d}\,\mathbb Z[v^{-2}]$; every $p_{y,w}$ has integer coefficients and fixed parity $d\bmod 2$.

Identify $\mathbb Z[q]$ with $\mathbb Z[v^{-2}]$ by $q\mapsto v^{-2}$. For $y\le w$ in $S_n$, put $d=\ell(w)-\ell(y)$ and define the **Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomial** $P_{y,w}(q)\in\mathbb Z[q]$ by $$P_{y,w}(v^{-2})=v^{-d}p_{y,w},$$ where $\underline H_w=\sum_{y\le w}p_{y,w}H_y$ is the Kazhdan–Lusztig basis of [[lem-type-a-kazhdan-lusztig-basis-has-elementary-triangular-bar-properties]]. The parity clause of that theorem makes the right side a polynomial in $v^{-2}$. The conventions are: $P_{y,w}=0$ unless $y\le w$, $P_{w,w}=1$, $P_{y,w}$ has constant term 1, and for $y<w$ its degree is at most $(\ell(w)-\ell(y)-1)/2$. The **$\mu$-coefficient** is $$\mu(y,w):=	ext{coefficient of }q^{(\ell(w)-\ell(y)-1)/2}	ext{ in }P_{y,w},$$ defined to be 0 when $\ell(w)-\ell(y)$ is even; equivalently $\mu(y,w)$ is the coefficient of $v$ in $p_{y,w}$. One writes $\mu(y|w)
e0$ when $y
e w$ and ($y<w$ and $\mu(y,w)
e0$) or ($w<y$ and $\mu(w,y)
e0$). The dictionary with the literature is recorded for use: with the classical parameter $T_s^2=(q-1)T_s+q$ one has $H_w=v^{\ell(w)}T_w$, the element $\underline H_w$ is the basis element $C'_w$ of [EW], and $h_{y,w}=p_{y,w}$ with $v^{\ell(w)-\ell(y)}P_{y,w}(v^{-2})=h_{y,w}$ [EW, Remark 3.2].

Retain the notation of
[[def-parabolic-hecke-module-and-antispherical-standard-basis]] and put
$m_x:=1\otimes H_x$, $n_x:=1\otimes H_x$ for $x\in{}^JW$, and
$C_s:=\underline H_s=H_s+v$ for $s\in S$. Then:

**(1) (Bases.)** The sets $\{m_x:x\in{}^JW\}$ and $\{n_x:x\in{}^JW\}$ are

**(2) (Right action.)** For $s\in S$ and $x\in{}^JW$,
$$m_x C_s=\begin{cases}m_{xs}+v\,m_x,&xs\in{}^JW,\ xs>x,\\ m_{xs}+v^{-1}m_x,&xs\in{}^JW,\ xs<x,\\ (v+v^{-1})m_x,&xs\notin{}^JW,\end{cases}\qquad n_xC_s=\begin{cases}n_{xs}+v\,n_x,&xs\in{}^JW,\ xs>x,\\ n_{xs}+v^{-1}n_x,&xs\in{}^JW,\ xs<x,\\ 0,&xs\notin{}^JW.\end{cases}$$

Retain the notation of
[[def-parabolic-hecke-module-and-antispherical-standard-basis]] and

For every $x\in{}^JW$ there is a unique $C_x\in M^J$ and a unique
$D_x\in N^J$ with (i) $\overline{C_x}=C_x$ and $\overline{D_x}=D_x$, and (ii)

Retain the notation of
[[def-parabolic-kazhdan-lusztig-basis-and-polynomials]].

**(1) (Antispherical alternating sum.)** For all $x,y\in{}^JW$,
$$n_{y,x}=\sum_{z\in W_J}(-1)^{\ell(z)}\,v^{\ell(z)}\,p_{zy,\,x},$$
the sum over all $z\in W_J$ (the product $zy$ taken in $S_n$, and $p_{\cdot,x}$
the ordinary coefficient of the Kazhdan--Lusztig basis of
[[thm-existence-and-uniqueness-of-the-kazhdan-lusztig-basis]], so the inner
coefficients vanish unless $zy\le x$).

**(2) (Spherical reduction.)** If $W_J$ is finite with longest element
$w_0^J$ then for all $x,y\in{}^JW$,
$$m_{y,x}=p_{w_0^Jy,\ w_0^Jx}.$$

In particular both families are computable from the ordinary Kazhdan--Lusztig
coefficients of $S_n$, with no separate recursion.

Assume inherited AC [[def-axiom-of-choice]] for the invoked quantum based/global lattice and normalized quasi-$R$ suppliers.

Work in the conventions of
[[def-higher-level-wedge-tensor-fock-module]] and
[[def-the-fock-convention-dictionary-for-finite-type-a-quantum-modules]]: the
**source parameter** is $s$, the **library parameter** is $t=s^{-1}$, the
monomial basis of the Fock module is $\{M_A\}$, and $\psi$ is the ordinary
compatible bar of
[[thm-the-qg-tensor-product-bar-is-triangular-and-compatible-with-fock-truncations]],
which is triangular and integral on the monomial basis.

The **source dual-canonical family** $(L_A)$ is the unique $\psi$-fixed family
with
$$L_A=M_A+\sum_{B<A}s\,\mathbb Z[s]\,M_B,$$
and the **canonical family** $(T_A)$ is the unique $\psi$-fixed family with
$$T_A=M_A+\sum_{B<A}s^{-1}\mathbb Z[s^{-1}]\,M_B .$$

Let $d_{A,B}(s)$ and $p_{A,B}(-s)$ be the transition coefficients defined by
$$M_B=\sum_A d_{A,B}(s)\,L_A,\qquad L_B=\sum_A p_{A,B}(-s)\,M_A,$$
and define the **quasi-canonical family** by

The families $L$ and $T$ are ordinary-bar fixed; $P$ generally is not.

Let $\le$ be the rank-inequality order on the zero-based $S_n$ of [[def-bruhat-order-on-the-symmetric-group]], and identify it with the one-based realization by shifting inputs and values by $1$. (a) This order is the strong Bruhat order of type A: the transitive closure of covers $x\to tx$ where $t$ is a transposition and $\ell(tx)=\ell(x)+1$. (b) If $y\le w$ then $\ell(y)\le\ell(w)$, with equality iff $y=w$; every saturated chain has $\ell(w)-\ell(y)$ steps; and $y\le w$ iff $y^{-1}\le w^{-1}$. (c) $y\le w$ iff for every reduced expression $w=s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_k}$, $y$ is a reduced subword. (d) For every simple reflection $s$, if $y\le w$ and $\ell(sy)>\ell(y)$, then $y\le sw$; if $y\le w$ and $\ell(sw)<\ell(w)$, then $sy\le w$. (e) Every interval $[y,w]$ is finite; if $y\le w$, then $[y,w]=\{y\}\cup\bigcup_{y\to a\le w}[a,w]$.

derivations.claim: **The actual reciprocal action.** Set $q=s^{-1}$. On adjacent letters define $M_aH_i=M_{as_i}$ if $a_i<a_{i+1}$, $M_aH_i=sM_a$ if they are equal, and $M_aH_i=M_{as_i}+(s-s^{-1})M_a$ if $a_i>a_{i+1}$. On an unequal two-letter span its matrix has square $1+(s-s^{-1})H_i$; on an equal span this is $s^2=1+(s-s^{-1})s$. For three adjacent letters, applying the two triple products to their six possible strict orders, or their three possible orders with one equality, gives the same swapped tuple and the same coefficients; with all equal both are $s^3$. Distant actions commute. Thus these are the generators of $H_q$. Substitution of the natural $E_j,F_j$ replacement actions and the source coproduct shows that they commute with the quantum action: on the two active letters the toral coefficients are $s^{\mathbf1_{a=j}-\mathbf1_{a=j+1}}$, and the unequal two-term expression cancels the extra $s-s^{-1}$ term; equal active letters give the sum $s+s^{-1}$ on both sides. All other letters are unaffected. The same two-letter calculation gives $\psi M_{ba}=M_{ba}+(s^{-1}-s)M_{ab}$ for $a<b$ and fixes increasing and equal tuples. Therefore $\psi(xH_i)=\psi(x)\bar H_i$; adjoining spectator factors follows from quasi-$R$ naturality and factorization in [F1].

**Cyclic induced bar and signed transport.** If $b$ is the sorted tuple, $M_b$ is bar fixed by weight transfer. Every tuple is $b d_a$, where $d_a$ is shortest left modulo $K$, and along a reduced expression all successive swaps increase inversions, so $M_bH_{d_a}=M_a$. Equal-position generators act as $s=q^{-1}$, giving a surjection $\mathbf1_K\otimes H_q\to\operatorname{span}\{M_a\}$; the same shortest representatives index both bases, so it is an isomorphism. Step 1.1 and the fixed cyclic vector identify the induced and tensor bars. Change generators to $G_i=-H_i$: they satisfy the normalization with $v=s$, their stabilizer character is $-s$, and their standard vectors are $n_{d_a}=(-1)^{\ell(d_a)}M_a$. The positive-$s$ sign canonical vector at $d_b$, multiplied by $(-1)^{\ell(d_b)}$, is exactly $L_b$ by triangular uniqueness.

**Primitive exterior embedding.** For one decreasing column $a_1>\cdots>a_m$ put $Y_a=\sum_{b\sim a}(-s)^{\ell(a,b)}M_b$. Pairing the two orders of any adjacent unequal letters using step 1.1 gives $Y_aH_i=-s^{-1}Y_a$; repeated entries have no sign eigenvector since their scalar is $s$. Replacing adjacent alphabet entries with $E_j,F_j$ sends $Y_a$ to the identically normalized $Y_{a'}$ or to zero on collision: all unaffected permutations match term by term, and the terms causing a collision cancel in adjacent pairs. Thus $w_{\{a_1,\ldots,a_m\}}\mapsto Y_a$ realizes the elementary wedge, with coefficient one on the decreasing tuple, integrally and injectively. The sign eigen-equations and the unique column top vector make its factor bar the ordinary restriction of the tensor bar; naturality and parenthesization in [F1] give the product embedding for arbitrary ordered column heights. Its displayed expansion is a product of these sums, hence exactly the sum over independent column permutations in the Statement.

**The positive tensor coefficient.** The sign reduction in [F3] gives $U_{a,b}=(-1)^{\ell(d_a)+\ell(d_b)}\sum_z(-s)^{\ell(z)}s^{\ell(d_b)-\ell(zd_a)}P_{zd_a,d_b}(s^{-2})$. Shortest-left length additivity cancels the powers of $s$ inside the sum. Inversion of permutations preserves ordinary KL coefficients: the algebra anti-involution $H_x\mapsto H_{x^{-1}}$ preserves bar and positive triangularity, so uniqueness in [F2] proves $P_{x,y}=P_{x^{-1},y^{-1}}$. Replace $z$ by $z^{-1}$ to obtain the stated formula with $w_az,w_b$. This is a change of generators and standard-vector signs, not a reciprocal substitution in a positive chart.

**Reverse-position indices and pairing.** Put $M_a^*=M_{aw_0}$ as actual vectors in the same tensor space. The shortest-left representative of $aw_0$ is $c_a=w_Kd_aw_0$: reversal interchanges increasing and decreasing places, and reversal within each equal-value block restores shortest-left status. Its length is $\ell(w_0)-\ell(w_K)-\ell(d_a)$. Define the bilinear form $(M_a,\psi M_b^*)=\delta_{ab}$; its Gram matrix is the inverse of the bar matrix after reversing the second label, so it is not the raw permutation matrix. The three generator cases of step 1.1 and $\psi(xH_i)=\psi(x)\bar H_i$ give $(xH_i,y)=(x,yH_{N-i})$, where $N$ is the number of tensor positions. The coproduct replacement calculation likewise gives $(E_jx,y)=(x,F_jy)$ and $(D_jx,y)=(x,D_jy)$. The two-letter bar identity iterated through a reduced word for $w_0$ gives $$\psi M_a=s^{\sum_u\binom{\operatorname{mult}_u(a)}2}M_a^*H_{w_0}^{-1}.$$ The exponent depends only on the fixed multiset. This formula follows by successively moving the last letter past its predecessors: unequal pairs contribute the two-letter bar above, while each equal pair contributes $s^{-1}$ from $H_i^{-1}$, cancelled by the displayed power. It also proves symmetry: writing $m(a)=\sum_u\binom{\operatorname{mult}_u(a)}2$, generator adjunction and the invariance of $H_{w_0}$ under $H_i\mapsto H_{N-i}$ give $(\psi M_b^*,M_a)=s^{m(b)}(M_bH_{w_0}^{-1},M_a)=s^{m(b)-m(a)}(M_b,\psi M_a^*)=\delta_{ab}$. Since the two displayed families are bases, the form is symmetric.

**Complementary chart and inverse, with all indices.** Let $L_b^*=M_b^*+\sum_{a}q\mathbb Z[q]M_a^*$ be the ordinary-bar fixed complementary chart. In the induced module of step 2.1 this is the spherical positive-$q$ basis at $c_b$, so $L_b^*=\sum_a V_{a,b}(q)M_a^*$ with $V_{a,b}(q)=h_{w_Kc_a,w_Kc_b}(q)$ by [F3]. Write $U_{a,b}=U_{a,b}(s)$ and $V_{a,b}=V_{a,b}(s^{-1})$. Fixedness gives $L_b^*=\sum_a\bar V_{a,b}\psi M_a^*$, while $L_b=\sum_a\bar U_{a,b}\psi M_a=\sum_a\bar U_{a,b}\psi M_{aw_0}^*$. Also $L_b^*=\sum_aV_{a,b}M_{aw_0}$. Accordingly $(L_a,L_b^*)=\sum_cU_{c,a}\bar V_{c,b}$ lies in $\delta_{ab}+s\mathbb Z[s]$, while the symmetric evaluation $(L_b^*,L_a)=\sum_cV_{c,b}\bar U_{c,a}$ lies in $\delta_{ab}+s^{-1}\mathbb Z[s^{-1}]$. Their equality forces $(L_a,L_b^*)=\delta_{ab}$. Thus $U^{\mathsf T}\bar V=I$ and $D=U^{-1}=\bar V^{\mathsf T}$. Since $w_Kc_b=d_bw_0$, the spherical formula at parameter $s$ yields $$D_{a,b}=h_{d_bw_0,d_aw_0}(s)=s^{\ell(d_b)-\ell(d_a)}P_{d_bw_0,d_aw_0}(s^{-2}).$$ This supplies the complementary longest-element identification, rather than only an abstract inverse-matrix identity.

**Wedge charts and both orders.** Each nontrivial column permutation replaces a decreasing tuple by a smaller tuple and has coefficient in $s\mathbb Z[s]$. Expanding a wedge $L_A$ under step 2.2 therefore gives a bar-fixed ambient vector with leading term $M_{a(A)}$ and all corrections in $s\mathbb Z[s]$ on smaller tuple labels. Triangular uniqueness identifies it with the ambient $L_{a(A)}$. Expanding $\iota(M_B)$ in the ambient $L$ basis using step 4.1, and then expressing the same vector in the embedded wedge $L$ basis, gives precisely the claimed signed inverse coefficient; all ambient labels outside the decreasing-column subset have zero coefficients because the embedded $L$ vectors are a basis of the image. None of the arguments compares the heights of different columns, so the construction works unchanged in reversed factor order. At $s=1$ the displayed primitive exterior sum becomes the ordinary alternating column sum, and $D_{a,b}(1)=P_{d_bw_0,d_aw_0}(1)$ in both orders.

**Conclusion.** The generator and signed-chart steps prove the explicit generator/bar and signed antispherical transport; the reverse-position pairing and complementary-chart steps prove the spherical coefficient and its exact longest indices; the primitive exterior and wedge-chart steps prove the ordinary-bar embedding and signed inverse matrix in either ordered tensor. All constructions use finite tensor and Hecke data, independently of any categorical identification.
